#5185. XRP Price Was Worth Less Than a Penny When GTA 5 Launched: Could GTA 6 See It Hit $100?

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

XRP price was trading below one cent when Grand Theft Auto V arrived in September 2013. Thirteen years later, Rockstar is preparing to release GTA 6, while XRP has grown into one of the largest cryptos. XRP is a financial giant today.

The comparison is striking. On September 17, 2013, the day GTA V launched, XRP was trading at $0.009613. Today, XRP trades near $0.95, representing a price gain of almost 100 times from that launch-day price.

But can XRP deliver another extraordinary rally as GTA 6 arrives? A $100 price target would turn a relatively small crypto investment into a fortune, but it would also require XRP to reach a market valuation never seen before in the crypto industry.

When GTA V introduced players to Los Santos in 2013, XRP was still largely flying under the radar. Its price sat below one cent, and its market cap was ranging around $75 million. Then the following years changed everything.

XRP broke above $0.10 in May 2017 before accelerating during the historic crypto bull market. By December 2017, the token had crossed $1 and continued climbing toward its January 2018 all-time high of $3.84.

That is an extraordinary transformation from its GTA V launch-day price. A $1,000 investment at $0.009613 would have purchased more than 100,000 XRP. At $3.84, that position would have been worth nearly $400,000. Something that only crypto can do.

However, XRP’s journey was far from smooth. The token endured successive bear markets, regulatory uncertainty, and the SEC’s lawsuit against Ripple in December 2020. Its recovery eventually pushed XRP back toward record territory in 2025, when it reached $3.65.

Now, XRP is trading around $0.95, substantially below its previous peaks. Will another major recovery begin before GTA 6 is released?

Rockstar’s GTA 6 arrives more than 13 years after GTA V, creating an interesting milestone for XRP investors. XRP has experienced multiple market cycles during the same period, transforming from a sub-penny asset into a major digital currency.

XRP currently has 63.5 billion tokens in circulation. At $100 per token, its market capitalization would reach $6.35 trillion. That would put XRP among the most valuable financial assets in the world, exceeding the market capitalization of most publicly traded companies.

The bullish argument rests on XRP’s potential to capture a much larger share of institutional payments, cross-border settlements, and digital asset liquidity. Ripple has spent years building financial infrastructure around the XRP Ledger, while institutional interest in crypto investment products continues to develop.

A stronger crypto market could also provide the liquidity needed for another substantial XRP rally. But XRP would need considerably more capital, adoption, and sustained demand to justify a multi-trillion-dollar valuation.

The historical comparison remains fascinating. XRP went from less than a penny when GTA V launched to several dollars during subsequent crypto cycles. People probably didn’t believe XRP would reach where it is now.

#5182. Bitcoin Demand Dries Up as Miners Prepare to Dump 2,077 BTC: Is More Selling Pressure Coming for BTC?

Bitcoin demand weakens as miners transfer 2,077 BTC to exchanges; Antpool accounting for 97% ahead of an estimated 8% mining difficulty cut.

Bitcoin (BTC) demand is showing signs of weakness as miners move more coins to cryptocurrency exchanges. CryptoQuant recorded 2,077 BTC in miner-to-exchange transfers on November 10, approximately 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. The move comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum and the network approaches an estimated 8% reduction in mining difficulty.

The latest figures raise concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as demand indicators weaken across spot and derivatives markets.

Meanwhile, miners could soon receive some relief from lower network difficulty.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

“Leverage is being unwound, but spot demand has not recovered sustainably.” – By @xwinfinance pic.twitter.com/n03axjQKqt

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

#5181. MIT Review Acclaims zk-SNARKs, but zk-STARKs May Steal the Show

Updated look back: this article revisits a 2018 story with what has happened since.

The short version: STARKs took a large share of the stage, SNARKs adapted, and Bulletproofs found a narrower job. Here is how the three compare and how the story played out.

A zero-knowledge proof lets you prove that a statement is true without showing the data behind it. MIT's examples were proving you are over 18 without giving your birth date, or proving you can afford a payment without showing your balance.

The idea is old. According to ethereum.org, it first appeared in a 1985 paper. What changed was that it became usable. MIT's entry, written by Mike Orcutt, credited much of that progress to Zcash, a currency launched in late 2016, and listed Zcash, JPMorgan Chase and ING as key players.

The same entry named two drawbacks. zk-SNARKs were slow and heavy to compute, and they needed a "trusted setup". It added that researchers were already looking for alternatives without those problems, but did not name any.

zk-SNARK stands for zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge. "Succinct" is the selling point. Zcash's documentation says a proof is only a few hundred bytes and can be checked in a few milliseconds, even for a very large computation.

That is what makes shielded Zcash transactions possible. The transaction is encrypted on the blockchain, yet the network can still confirm that it follows the rules.

The cost is the setup. Early SNARKs needed a one-time ceremony that produced public parameters. The ceremony also produced secret randomness, and Zcash's own documentation says anyone who kept it could forge proofs and create counterfeit coins. Zcash ran two multi-party ceremonies, one for its Sprout version and one for Sapling, so that no single person held the secret. Users still had to trust that at least one participant destroyed their share.

The STARK paper, "Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity", was submitted to the IACR ePrint archive on January 10, 2018 by Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh and Michael Riabzev. Its title states the three goals.

Transparent means no trusted setup. STARKs use public randomness, so there is no secret to leak.

Post-quantum refers to the underlying math. Ethereum.org explains that SNARKs depend on elliptic curve cryptography, which a future quantum computer may break, while STARKs rely only on collision-resistant hash functions.

Scalable means the work of checking a proof grows far more slowly than the computation being proved.

The trade-off is size. STARK proofs are larger, and ethereum.org notes that this makes them more expensive to verify on Ethereum. Figures quoted in the Ethereum Stack Exchange thread that cites this article give a sense of scale: about 288 bytes for a SNARK against about 45,000 bytes for a STARK in one comparison, and "hundreds of kilobytes" in one developer's real project. Those numbers depend heavily on the computation, so treat them as orders of magnitude.

Bulletproofs came out of Stanford in 2017, from Benedikt Bünz, Jonathan Bootle, Dan Boneh, Andrew Poelstra, Pieter Wuille and Greg Maxwell. Like STARKs, they need no trusted setup.

They were designed for one job: proving that a hidden amount in a confidential transaction falls within a valid range. The Stanford project page says they cut that proof from over 10 kB to under 1 kB. It also says a Bulletproof takes longer to verify than a SNARK, which is why they are not used for proving large computations.

Monero added Bulletproofs in its October 2018 network upgrade. Its documentation reports that average transaction size fell by at least 80 percent.

Partly. Three things happened after 2018.

STARKs reached production. Eli Ben-Sasson, the paper's first author, co-founded StarkWare with Alessandro Chiesa and Uri Kolodny. The company used STARKs first in StarkEx, a scaling service for individual clients, and then in Starknet, which launched its Alpha on Ethereum mainnet in November 2021. Starknet's documentation describes it as a permissionless validity rollup that settles on Ethereum using STARK proofs.

SNARKs fixed their own weakness. PLONK, published in August 2019 by Ariel Gabizon, Zachary Williamson and Oana Ciobotaru, is a universal SNARK: one setup can serve many different programs instead of one ceremony per program. Halo went further. Zcash says Halo removes the trusted setup entirely, and its Orchard shielded protocol, activated with the NU5 upgrade in May 2022, runs on the Halo 2 proving system.

That last point matters for the old "SNARKs need a trusted setup" comparison. It was accurate in 2018. It no longer holds for every SNARK.

The fair verdict: STARKs did not push SNARKs aside, but they did prove that transparency and hash-based security work at scale. The choice today is less about which family wins and more about what you need: the smallest proof, no setup, or protection against quantum attacks.

#5180. SOL Eyes New Bullish Era as Solana Ditches ‘Beta’ Label After Six Years and Embraces Protocol Version 1.0

Solana has officially turned a major page in its history, dropping the long-standing ‘beta’ tag after more than six years and adopting protocol version 1.0. The milestone marks a significant step in the network’s evolution as it moves beyond its experimental phase, with ongoing efforts to improve transaction speed, finality, and overall performance. The development could also strengthen Solana’s appeal to developers and institutional players, raising fresh questions about whether SOL is poised for a new bullish chapter.

Solana has officially retired its six-year-old “mainnet beta” designation, with the network’s foundation saying the rebranding highlights the significant strides made since the blockchain first launched in March 2020.

“Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience,” the Solana foundation wrote in a Monday statement. “That progress continues with this simplification of nomenclature.”

The foundation emphasized that Solana has operated as a fully live network since its launch, arguing that retaining the beta designation had become outdated. It noted that the label, traditionally associated with technology still in its early testing stages, no longer accurately represented a blockchain already processing transactions and hosting active applications.

According to the Solana Foundation, the reclassification requires no action from users. Existing SOL holdings, account balances, and transaction histories will remain unchanged despite the protocol’s transition to version 1.0.

The foundation also advised developers and validator operators to stick to the specific instructions accompanying software releases, stressing that the new protocol designation does not mean all network upgrades or improvements become active automatically.

Solana’s move to protocol version 1.0 comes as the network continues pursuing major infrastructure improvements, with Alpenglow and Firedancer among its most closely watched developments. Both initiatives aim to strengthen Solana’s performance, reliability, and ability to support growing on-chain activity.

The first major milestone is Alpenglow, Solana’s new consensus protocol, which went live on mainnet on October 21. The upgrade targets transaction finality of approximately 150 milliseconds, a significant improvement from the previous 12.8-second timeframe. Transaction finality refers to the moment a blockchain permanently confirms a transaction, meaning it is considered settled and cannot be reversed under normal network conditions. Faster finality could make Solana more attractive for payments, decentralized finance, and institutional applications that require near-instant transaction settlement.

Meanwhile, Firedancer brings another important improvement through an independently developed validator client built by Jump Crypto. It provides an alternative to Solana’s existing Agave client, reducing the network’s dependence on a single software implementation. This client diversity could strengthen network resilience by limiting the risk that a bug affecting one implementation disrupts the entire blockchain.

The foundation added that the rebranding establishes a unified system for tracking Solana’s updates, allowing developers, validators, and infrastructure providers to identify protocol changes consistently, regardless of the software client they use.

#5176. CFTC Makes Historic Move With Blockchain Derivatives Approval

The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened historic doors for blockchain technology adoption in traditional financial markets as it approves exchange and clearinghouse applications for blockchain-based derivatives market infrastructure.

On Nov. 16, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig announced that the commission had given the green light to exchange (designated contract market or DCM) and clearinghouse (derivatives clearing organization or DCO) applications for a company using blockchain technology for the execution and settlement of derivatives contracts.

As per the official statement, Selig considers this a major step forward for U.S. financial markets. He said that blockchain-based market infrastructure is compatible with current U.S. financial regulations.

"This approval makes clear that there is a regulatory path for companies that want to innovate and use blockchain technology to modernize how derivatives are traded and settled,"  he elaborated.

Selig pointed out that the U.S. derivatives markets have seen a number of technological advancements, from physical trading floors to electronic trading platforms.

Now, with blockchain technology, he believes there is an opportunity to further modernize financial market infrastructure without losing regulatory oversight and investor protections.

Notably, there is no technical architecture requirement imposed on derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses under the CFTC's current regulatory framework.

Therefore, firms that leverage blockchain-based networks can apply for regulatory approval under the same set of rules and regulations that apply to traditional financial market participants.

However, Selig also clarified that blockchain adoption is not a license to escape regulatory oversight.

Companies will still need to comply with rules covering anti-money laundering (AML), client protections, market monitoring, risk mitigation and other measures designed to protect the integrity of financial markets.

Simply put, the CFTC is looking to bring blockchain technology into regulated derivatives market infrastructure while maintaining the same standards as traditional financial market participants.

For some time, the CFTC chairman has been pushing for a scenario where U.S. companies developing emerging financial technologies can operate in the country without having to look to international markets.

The latest developments further reinforce the message that the U.S. is open for business for companies building blockchain-based financial market infrastructure, according to Selig.

Malicious JavaScript code snippets were planted on the websites of 178 organizations.

The exploit originated inside Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform, a tool that many large companies use for A/B testing, which means showing users multiple versions of a page to determine which one is more effective.

Report URI estimates that on November 16 the code sat in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely snippets it crawled, and the real number is most likely higher.

Among the websites that could become victims of the hack are some of the largest names in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Fox News, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. BleepingComputer confirms that the script loads on many of them.

Essentially, the script's goal was to swap a wallet address on the page for the attacker's one, capture card numbers, take screenshots of pages and more. It was a whole stack of tools used to steal personal data, wallets and other assets.

According to Report URI, the attacker's wallets received about $7,040 within the first nine hours. That is a drop in the ocean considering the names involved, though the losses from card skimming are unknown. A card skimmer was added later that day, and a hidden iframe tried to load an iOS exploit chain on older iPhones.

Optimizely confirmed that an unauthorized party had exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation to add malicious JavaScript to certain customer projects. How the flaw worked is yet to be confirmed.

If successful, it could become one of the largest supply-chain attacks we have ever witnessed. Considering the attack came from a third party, we might see one of the largest service migrations in the world, as none of the third-party services and libraries can be trusted nowadays if used through an API.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain tasks to third-party providers all the time, so witnessing a similar situation in our field is more than a possibility.

For product owners: stay cautious and rethink the use of services prone to exploits. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

#5172. NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:

The yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

New tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

The formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every new token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics said the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a new proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to update their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

#5169. Xsolla ZK’s New Gas Token Aims to Let Digital Items Travel Between Games and Players

Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

Xsolla ZK, Inc. is introducing Xsolla Gas (XLA), the native token of Xsolla ZK — a blockchain network built for games. XLA is designed to pay the network fees that arise when players transfer or share eligible digital items on Xsolla ZK.

For players who’d rather not download and set up a separate wallet, Xsolla Gas Station, offered by Xsolla (USA), Inc., can cover those fees. There, players buy XLA-NT, a non-transferable gas credit used only to pay network fees on Xsolla ZK. (Xsolla Gas Station sells only XLA-NT.)

Players want more from the games and brands they follow, and developers want new ways to engage them. Digital items have evolved well beyond cosmetics — players now collect them from their favorite games. But letting players keep, share, and give away those items has long been complicated.

Most digital items today live on a single game’s backend. Players generally can’t transfer them to friends or carry them into another game, and the items simply vanish if a game shuts down. Blockchain-backed items stay with the players who collect them — but transferring them requires a network fee, which traditionally means setting up and managing a separate digital wallet and acquiring the right token to pay. That friction adds up.

Xsolla ZK is designed to remove that friction. Xsolla’s existing payment, monetization, and distribution products can now support blockchain-backed items — giving developers a new way to monetize and distribute digital items, and giving players new ways to keep them and pass them on.

Players use Xsolla Gas to cover the network fees required to transfer or share a digital item held in their Xsolla Backpack.

Xsolla Backpack is an inventory for the digital items a player owns. Items issued to the Backpack in transferable form are designed to remain available to the player even if the issuing game shuts down — and can be given to another player.

The intent is to put players in control of what happens to the eligible items they own. Digital items that remain on a game’s own backend continue to work exactly as they do today and can’t be transferred through Backpack.

Players who want to collect these items simply sign in to their account as usual — no seed phrase, no separate wallet setup. They cover network fees by buying XLA-NT gas credits through Xsolla Gas Station, using the payment methods they already know and prefer.

From there, players can collect eligible items they purchase or claim in their Backpack and share them with other players.

“Players should be able to share and gift digital items they own, anytime, anywhere, with anyone they know,” said Chris Hewish, President of Xsolla (USA). “Developers gain a new way to monetize their games, and players gain eligible digital items that are theirs to keep. When both sides win, the games do too. We are adding options inside the tools they already use, not asking anyone to change how they work.”

When a player wants to share or give away a digital item, the transaction runs on Xsolla ZK, the blockchain network, and the network fee is paid in Xsolla Gas. This lets players hold items and pass them on to others, and it’s designed to let them carry items between supported games.

Players can cover the fee themselves in XLA or XLA-NT, while developers and partners can use XLA to pay network fees for their own item activity.

More than 1,500 game teams use Xsolla (USA)’s tools and services to monetize and distribute games. Those tools are designed to work with Xsolla ZK to support the transfer of eligible digital items — and Xsolla Backpack and Xsolla Gas Station are now available without additional development for teams using compatible Xsolla (USA) products, integrating directly with existing player and payment flows.

Studios, publishers, brands, and players can learn more about Xsolla Gas Station at x.la/gas. Developers building games, wallets, marketplaces, and item services on Xsolla ZK can find network documentation, developer tools, and integration paths at xsolla.org.

Readers can also complete a short Xsolla Quest at xsolla.pro/xsolla-zk-quest to learn more about Xsolla Gas, Xsolla Gas Station, and Xsolla Backpack.

What is Xsolla Quest? Xsolla Quest lets people complete a few simple steps on an Xsolla page to receive an item.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on Nov. 16, and the proposal lowers the maximum annual issuance of NEAR Protocol from 2.5% to 1.6%. On Tuesday, the price of NEAR dipped to $3.12 in the morning and then went back up to $3.26.

HSP-029 was written by Sal Ternullo, CEO of SVRN, and opened for forum discussion on Oct. 7. The vote closed on Nov. 2, and 99.96% of the veNEAR cast was in favor of the proposal; no veNEAR was cast against it. The Security Council's 14-day window to veto the proposal closed on Nov. 16 with no veto, according to House of Stake.

This is the second inflation cut for NEAR in just over a year. In October 2025, the maximum issuance was halved from the original 5% to 2.5%, and in September 2026, the realized issuance stood at 2.45%, according to HSP-029.

At 1.6%, NEAR will have "one of the lowest annual issuance rates among major blockchains," House of Stake said.

According to House of Stake, the reduction will start one quarter after ratification, and validators still have to adopt the protocol upgrade. The issuance cap will reach 1.6% after 24 months.

Ternullo estimated in HSP-029 that NEAR will avoid issuing 11.8 million tokens over two years. At the current price, these tokens would be worth around $38.5 million.

The proposal also calculated that the staking yield of NEAR will go down from around 5.27% to around 3.37% if the staking ratio stays the same. More than half of all NEAR is not staked, according to House of Stake.

Ledger, a crypto wallet firm, said it had experienced a security incident related to Optimizely, a third-party service used on its official website, but reassured its users about the security of their devices and private keys.

In a post, Ledger said it was aware of a security incident impacting Optimizely, a third-party service provider used by many other sites as well.

We are aware of a security incident affecting Optimizely, a third-party service used on https://t.co/d2pWxdG49X, alongside numerous other websites. Our team has remediated the issue, and the malicious code is no longer being served through our website. This incident does not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices. Your private keys remain protected by your Ledger device. For more information from Optimizely: https://t.co/CxzmBxYadb

Website optimization platform Optimizely said it had discovered and contained a security incident affecting some of its Web Experimentation customers on November 16, 2026. Optimizely stated that the vulnerable path has now been blocked, the injected code has been removed, and customers have been contacted directly.

Along these lines, Ledger confirmed that its team had remediated the issue and that the malicious code was no longer being served through its website.

Ledger emphasizes that the incident did not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices and that user private keys remain protected by their Ledger device, thus reassuring users that the incident had not compromised the core security of its wallet products.

According to researcher Scott Helme, on November 16, 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organizations' websites across several sectors through the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform. The websites included Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger, and Peacock.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed, with only 1 of the 188 infected snippets found, down from 169.

The main point is that trusted JavaScript is not always trustworthy. A third-party dependency can exploit a website without ever breaking the website's own code or infrastructure.

Citigroup has cut its 12-month projection for Bitcoin to $99,532 from $113,000, and that of Ethereum from $2,838 to $3,028.

Its reasons for the downgrade include a recent price slump, negative ETF flows and momentum indicators, lowered open interest, and mounting liquidations.

BTC has to maintain prices above the $60,000 support for it to reclaim 65,000, while Ethereum's floor lies at $1,705 with $1,800 as the next upward resistance.

Citigroup today trimmed its 12-month forecasts for Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), citing weaker institutional demand amid the recent market selloff.

For Bitcoin, the bank has lowered its target from $113,000, given on October 1, to $99,532. Meanwhile, Ethereum’s projection was shifted from an initial $3,028 to $2,838.

At press time, Bitcoin was trading at $62,769, while Ethereum traded at $1,759, with both having shed roughly 1.5% each in the day. The new targets now mean Bitcoin and Ethereum would have to surge 55% and 58% respectively from their current prices.

Led by Citigroup analyst Alex Saunders, the bank’s statement highlighted several reasons for its latest revision.

The first is that the two assets have declined since their last update, dipping more than 20% in the past month alone.

At the current price, Bitcoin is also well below its 200-day simple moving average, which sits between $72,283 and $72,795. Saunders cites this as the reason for downgrading Bitcoin’s short-term flow outlook to neutral.

ETF demand has also worsened, with November 17 flows for Bitcoin and Ethereum at -$242 million and -$26 million, respectively.

In the derivatives market, Ethereum futures have experienced the sharpest unwind. Total open interest is now at $9.12 billion, down $3 billion in under two weeks and now at its lowest level since October 2024.

Bitcoin futures market experienced a similar, albeit milder, contraction, falling more than 20% in the past week ($52.66 billion to $41.95 billion between November 9 and 18).

Even more, liquidations mounted to about $3.6 billion between November 13 and 15, while funding rates plunged to 0.0020% for Bitcoin and 0.0001% for Ethereum, both below the 0.005% baseline.

âBTC flows have turned into net outflows year-to-date, and ETH has recorded outflows in each of the last seven weeks, while futures positioning indicates a reduction in leverage across tokens.â

Citigroupâs latest update implies possible long-term recovery on a bumpy short-term path. For now, Bitcoin has to maintain above the $60,000 floor, and reclaim 65,000 to pace way for a $70,000 target.

Ethereum, on the other hand, has a lower support of $1,705 while facing an upward hurdle of $1,800. $1,900 is the initial recovery market, and $2,000 is the psychological support level. All these projections depend on ETF flows stabilizing and indicators turning positive.

The XRP reserves on Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange by registered global users, have plunged to a new multi-year low despite the token’s price capitulation.

On November 19, 2026, the XRP Ledger: Binance Reserve Simple Moving Average (SMA) hovered at about 2,574,399,498.99 tokens, according to data Coinpedia analyzed from CryptoQuant.

The gradual decline in XRP reserves on Binance signals a significant reduction in available sell-side supply. Furthermore, the exchange’s supply of the crypto asset has fallen from 3,465,765,422.9 tokens on April 8, 2024.

As a result, the XRP reserves on Binance have tumbled by nearly 26% over the past 32 months. Essentially, investors have been moving XRP from Binance, possibly to self-custodial wallets, signaling rising demand from holders.

Worth noting that the decline in XRP reserves to a new all-time low happens amid a heightened crypto bear market, indicating strong conviction.

At the time of reporting, XRP price was at $0.963, down more than 26% over the past 30 days. As such, the token’s market capitalization had contracted to $61.17 billion, with its 24-hour trading volume at roughly $1.94 billion.

The altcoin has faced a renewed downtrend despite heightened demand from investors, largely driven by heavy liquidation of long positions. Moreover, falling prices have forced long holders to sell their positions, thereby accelerating the decline through a long squeeze.

Notably, XRP investors moved their tokens from Binance at a faster rate over the past 30 days despite the price falling below $1, which could be a signal of a possible rebound. Consequently, reduced tokens available for trading on Binance could stir a fresh bull market in the near future.

#5151. Ripple’s RLUSD Supply Hits Record $2.7 Billion, With Ethereum Holding Majority Over XRP Ledger

RLUSD supply has climbed to $2.7 billion, indicating rising on-chain demand for its stablecoin, which operates mostly on Ethereum, according to data.

Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin has achieved another milestone. Its total market supply has reached $2.7 billion, making a new high level in circulation, according to data reported on the X platform. RLUSD supply climbed to the $2.7 billion record on Sunday, Nov. 15, a 57% rise from the $1.72 billion mark seen on Sept. 14, data revealed.

The market supply of the Ripple-backed stablecoin has surged to a new ATH, exceeding the previous $1.72 billion milestone set in September. According to the data, RLUSD’s circulating supply currently stands at $2.7 billion, up from the $1.2 billion level reached in January. This rise signals an expansion of RLUSD’s liquidity across the wider blockchain ecosystem.

The supply expansion indicates rising demand for RLUSD as global customers gradually embrace the stablecoin for payments and DeFi applications. This surge positions RLUSD as a ‘digital dollar’ that allows users to execute cross-border payments and on-chain settlements.

The growth is pushing RLUSD higher into the stablecoin market. Now, the asset ranks as the 7th-largest stablecoin by market supply. The more supply means deeper liquidity across the public blockchain ecosystem, supporting cross-border payments and on-chain utility.

The Ripple-focused institutional stablecoin has reached another milestone, increasing its market supply to $2.7 billion. Interestingly, a large amount of this freshly issued liquidity operates on external public blockchains, not within the XRP Ledger network.

Metrics show that a large share of the new RLUSD supply sits on Ethereum, with Ethereum holding more than those in the XRP Ledger. This indicates rising use of Ethereum as a liquidity and settlement network for the stablecoin, while RLUSD continues to expand across protocols.

On-chain data indicates that out of the $2.7 billion in RLUSD circulation, about $1.73 billion runs on Ethereum. The XRP Ledger holds around $855 million, representing about 30% of the circulation.

Over time, Ethereum’s share of the supply has risen to about 60%. This shift is because Ethereum offers a deeper DeFi market, including lending and more. XRP Ledger is closer to activating its native lending infrastructure.

Elon Musk said on Friday, November 13, that he is signing the Jensen Huang petition, an open letter asking Nvidia’s board to bring back its former chief executive. Huang resigned a day earlier, after reports of extramarital affairs.

By Monday, the “Stand with Jensen” letter had more than 160,000 signatures. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick have also backed it. The letter asks the board to reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts.

Tech executives are pushing to reinstate Jensen Huang, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly opposes his return.

A petition backing Huang has drawn 175,000 signatures.

Yet prediction markets give Huang just an 18%… pic.twitter.com/BZl5KheVnq

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 16, 2026

We matched Polymarket’s odds of Huang’s return with a 24/7 Nvidia stock contract on Hyperliquid. Musk’s post lifted the odds but barely moved the stock. A sharper jump in the odds on Sunday evening did: the stock rose 3% within two hours, then gave it all back by Monday.

So how is Nvidia’s stock reacting, one day before earnings?

Musk posted on X that “a petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.” He had said earlier that hiring Huang would be “an honor.”

The petition is hosted at standwithjensen.com. Signers report their own job titles, and the site does not verify them. More than 7,500 say they work at the company, about 18% of its staff.

The company says it is choosing a search firm for the CEO role and has not formally approached any candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress runs the company in the meantime.

The Jensen Huang petition has moved the odds more than the stock. Musk’s backing barely shifted the price, and Sunday’s jump faded within a day. Tuesday’s earnings, the first under Kress, are likely to matter more to Nvidia shares than any petition.

#5142. 178 Websites Infected in Major Optimizely Hack: Crypto Wallets Targeted, but Bitcoin Barely Reacted

Optimizely attack infects 178 websites, steals crypto and card data, and exposes users to wallet-address swaps and iPhone exploits.

An Optimizely attack on Monday, November 16, planted crypto-stealing code on the websites of 178 organizations, including Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN. The malicious script swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed card numbers, and tried to break into iPhones for about 19 hours before it was cleaned up.

BREAKING: A cyberattack hit 178 major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, BBC, Fox News, HSBC, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA and Air France-KLM, by loading malware on the Optimizely Web platform, exposing visitors to scripts built to steal payment data and exploit iOS…

— The Hormuz Letter (@HormuzLetter) November 17, 2026

Optimizely is a tool companies use to test different versions of their web pages. An attacker slipped code into the scripts it serves, so every site that loaded them ran the malware.

We traced the attacker’s Bitcoin wallet. It received five payments worth about $5,500, and one victim alone sent nearly 90% of it. Bitcoin barely moved while the attack ran.

So what happened, and what is the real impact of hacks like this one?

Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI found the code and published a full breakdown. The attacker wrote it into a settings field in customers’ Optimizely projects, so it was served from Optimizely’s own servers and looked legitimate.

Optimizely said it “secured affected user accounts and added protections against further unauthorized code delivery.” Report URI found no sign that Ledger hardware wallets themselves were breached. The danger was on the website, where a copied address could be swapped before a user pasted it.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

Report URI listed the attacker’s wallets. We checked the Bitcoin one on mempool.space, the public Bitcoin block explorer.

The Optimizely attack’s impact was tiny, and the market ignored it. Bitcoin is near $64,300 after its weekend low of $62,006, and that slide came from wider selling, not this attack.

EXPLORE: Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 Billion in 2026, More Than Triple 2025: How Did Bitcoin and Ether React?

The money stolen in the Optimizely attack is small, but the method is the year’s most damaging one. We sorted DefiLlama’s 2026 hack list by attack type. Attacks on websites and infrastructure, rather than on smart contracts, are now the costliest category:

These attacks hit users where no wallet setting can protect them. The fix is on the user’s side: check the address on the hardware wallet’s screen before signing, send a small test transfer first, and keep phones updated.

On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $64,326. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $76,208, and its 200-day EMA at $75,864.

The Optimizely attack did not move Bitcoin, and the attacker walked away with about $7,000. Its real cost is trust: when a hardware-wallet maker’s own website can serve malware for hours, checking every address on the device is no longer optional.

Board chair Harvey Jones spoke about the search for a permanent CEO, alongside senior leaders including Ian Buck, who heads the hyperscale and high-performance computing business and is the top pick on Kalshi to become the next CEO. Co-founder Chris Malachowsky and engineering chief Jonah Alben also addressed staff. The meeting comes as some employees push for Huang’s return, with one senior employee reportedly warning the board it could lose irreplaceable talent. Others welcomed the greater visibility into leadership. The board has said it unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and will not reinstate him.

#5136. Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Holder Wakes Up After 15 Years, Refuting $250 Billion ‘Lost’ Claim

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

A Bitcoin address that had not moved coins since February 2011 transferred 75 BTC on Nov. 17, according to Galaxy Research. At the current price of $64,935 per BTC, the coins are worth around $4.87 million.

The address is listed as a defendant in a $250 billion lawsuit in New York Supreme Court, in which the plaintiffs are trying to have early Bitcoin wallets declared "lost." Galaxy Research said that several other addresses from the same list have also moved coins in 2026.

According to Galaxy Research analysts, early on Nov. 17, in block 976,209, the address 1ALpEWtXApR19hLXvcG8NfkPyGsUMhFPMS sent coins for the first time. It was first funded on Feb. 8, 2011. At that time, Bitcoin was trading at about $0.90. After 15.8 years, the coins went to an unknown address with a 399-satoshi fee, or about 26 cents, for a paper gain of more than 7,000,000%.

Onchain databases list the wallet as Noah Doe #3409 (Salomon Client Dusted). That label is how it ended up among the defendants in the high-profile case ABC Company, XYZ Company, and Noah Doe v. John Does 1–39,069.

According to the lawsuit, an anonymous plaintiff using the pseudonym Noah Doe and two companies want the rights to 39,069 Bitcoin wallets that have not moved coins for more than five years. The plaintiffs said that these wallets hold about 3.8 million BTC, and at the current price, the coins are worth around $250 billion.

The plaintiffs filed the lawsuit under New York's lost-and-found law, Article 7-B of the Personal Property Law. Under the law, a person who finds lost property has to give it to the police, and the property goes to the finder if the owner does not claim it in time. In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs valued each address at less than $10, and they argued that the waiting period for such items was one year.

They "found" dormant addresses with an algorithm, saved them onto USB flash drives and took them to the New York Police Department (NYPD). Then they served the owners on the blockchain, through microtransactions with embedded messages (OP_RETURN). The practice is known as "dusting," and the campaign is tied to Salomon Brothers Strategic Advisors. Once the waiting period ran out, the plaintiffs asked the court to recognize the coins as theirs.

The case has been put on hold several times over motions to dismiss and amicus curiae briefs from outside experts. At a hearing on Sept. 8, the Bitcoin Policy Institute asked to intervene as a defendant, and The Digital Chamber asked to join the case as amicus curiae. Galaxy Research described it as a case "in which anonymous plaintiffs are seeking to claim legal title over Satoshi's coins."

Galaxy Research's Will Owens, who attended the hearing, said that The Digital Chamber's arguments were "well pleaded" and that "the judge sounded sympathetic to them."

Critics of the lawsuit argue that Article 7-B was written for things you can pick up and hand over for safekeeping. It wasn't written for blockchain records when the "finder" doesn't hold the private keys.

In September, Galaxy head of research Alex Thorn also said that the Lost and Found Property Law includes "protection from 'Noah Doe-style' dormancy attacks on legal ownership."

#5135. Binance Hacker Unleashes $137 Million ETH Dump, Swaps It for BTC

The exploiter recently moved 74,880 ETH ($136.8M) via THORchain and swapped it for Bitcoin.

On-chain reporters have identified massive flows from the wallet of the recent Binance hacker. The exploiter recently moved 74,880 ETH ($136.8M) via THORchain and swapped it for Bitcoin. The move is essentially a sizeable ETH dump, which can cause further trouble for the programmable digital currency amidst the ongoing slump in the crypto market.

While a considerable amount of their exploits has been frozen in place, especially USDT and USDC, on-chain BTC and ETH transfers are virtually impossible to block. Still, trackers are actively pursuing them. The total ETH holdings belonging to this hacker were initially 602,402 $ETH, but it now appears he is actively looking to swap it for Bitcoin.

The move marks the end of a relatively quiet period for the stolen Ethereum, which was seized during a 3-hour hacking episode that rocked Binance and the crypto world. All in all, $6.3 billion was stolen from the exchange’s hot wallets, and a huge chunk of it still lies in the wallets tied to the hacking entity. It was the largest crypto exploit in history by dollar value and has caused the market to lose more than 20% of its value since.

The use of cross-chain bridges like THORChain has reignited the debate around these automated, decentralized services. Broader industry scrutiny means these services could come under pressure in the near future. Already, US agencies like the FBI have urged the chain’s node operators to block addresses associated with the hack.

However, there is no solution to this loophole in sight. Critics argue that even if the Bitcoin and Ethereum connected to these exploit wallets cannot be touched in a decentralized economy, they should be prevented from using platforms like THORChain to try to mix and legitimize their illegitimate funds. Eventually, the crypto will end up in centralized exchanges, where it can be blocked and returned to the affected Binance exchange.

Furthermore, the popular use of these cross-chain bridges is influencing liquidity in THORChain pools and contributing to a broader market price squeeze. Initially, it was predicted that a large chunk of the stolen crypto would be frozen for some time, but the sudden exodus has put further pressure on the market, affecting smaller digital currencies more than larger ones.

Hopes of recovering the funds are not lost, as trackers continue to pursue them with the help of automation.

#5133. Ripple-Backed Evernorth Takes Massive $505 Million XRP Hit

Ripple-backed XRP treasury company Evernorth Holdings has disclosed a significant decrease in the book value of its crypto asset holdings, with total impairment charges amounting to around $505 million before going public on Nasdaq.

Per an SEC filing on Nov. 13, the 346.3 million XRP tokens that Evernorth Holdings owned had a book value of just $341.9 million as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This is compared to the firm's initial accounting of the crypto assets at roughly $846.6 million, with an average acquisition or contribution price of $2.44 per XRP. This represents a nearly 60% decline in book value.

As per the latest filing, Evernorth recorded around $271 million in XRP impairment charges in the first nine months of 2026. This is in addition to the $233.7 million in impairment charges recorded in 2025.

Interestingly, only $6.9 million of the recent impairment charges occurred in the third quarter.

This also explains why Evernorth's XRP assets had a book value so far below their market value at the end of September.

Evernorth calculates impairments based on the lowest observable intraday price of XRP for each batch of tokens acquired. Once the assets are written down, the company is unable to reverse the previous losses if the price rises.

For reference, on Sept. 30, XRP closed the day trading at around $1.49 on Coinbase. At that price, Evernorth's 346.3 million XRP tokens would have been worth roughly $516 million, much higher than the disclosed book value of $341.9 million.

The recent disclosure comes around a month after Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9. It started trading on Nasdaq under the symbol XRPN on Oct. 12.

Following the business combination, Evernorth held around 473 million XRP tokens and had also raised gross cash proceeds of around $300 million.

Its investors include Ripple, SBI Group, Arrington Capital, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

On Oct. 14, Evernorth announced collaborations with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo to implement institutional investment strategies starting in Q4 2026.

Meanwhile, its latest SEC filing did not include details on the amount of XRP deployed to generate yield or the returns generated from it.

#5131. Major Institutional Milestone for XRP: XRPL Becomes First Public Blockchain to Pass Global Financial Infrastructure Standards Assessment

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) has scored a major institutional milestone that could bolster its appeal to traditional financial institutions as demand for blockchain-based financial infrastructure grows.

The XRP Ledger Foundation has announced that the network is the first public, permissionless Layer-1 blockchain to have its Architecture and Resiliency principles independently verified under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The XRP Ledger’s latest achievement could mark an important step toward strengthening its position in the institutional blockchain market. On November 13, the independent attestation report detailing XRPL’s assessment under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit was released, highlighting the network’s willingness to measure its infrastructure against standards designed for traditional financial markets and emerging digital asset systems.

Notably, the XRP Ledger Foundation conducted a self-assessment covering all 10 principles, while blockchain security firm CertiK independently reviewed the supporting evidence for the Architecture and Resiliency principles. Its verification involved reviewing technical evidence—including code, system configurations, logs, and test results—to determine whether selected controls were implemented as described.

The development could give financial institutions a more structured reference point when evaluating XRPL for institutional-grade financial applications. However, the assessment does not amount to full GL1 certification or regulatory approval, meaning prospective institutional users will still need to conduct their own due diligence.

The Global Layer One initiative brings together leading financial institutions and policymakers to establish common standards for digital financial infrastructure. It aims to streamline cross-border transactions involving tokenized assets while ensuring that blockchain networks meet internationally recognized requirements for financial market infrastructure.

The latest development may strengthen the XRP Ledger’s prospects among traditional financial institutions considering blockchain-based financial solutions. Potential use cases include tokenized deposits, stablecoins, investment funds, and capital-market instruments. The GL1 assessment framework incorporates globally recognized financial market guidelines, drawing on CPMI-IOSCO principles and established digital asset control standards.

The review also provides institutions with a clearer framework for examining XRPL’s technical infrastructure, operational resilience, and suitability for financial applications. To maintain its relevance, the XRP Ledger Foundation intends to revisit the assessment periodically, taking into account future network improvements and changes in global industry requirements.

Bank of America has disclosed a position in an XRP exchange-traded fund in its latest quarterly 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing, dated Nov. 16, shows that the bank held 13,260 shares of the futures-based Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI), worth about $106,600, at the end of the third quarter.

Bank of America held 13,000 shares of the fund in the first quarter and 13,260 shares in the second quarter, according to its earlier 13F filings. The same filing lists more than $685 million in BlackRock's IBIT, $13.58 million in Bitwise and $950,000 in VanEck.

Seven major banks disclosed XRP fund holdings worth a total of $29.4 million in filings published between Nov. 9 and Nov. 16. Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed the largest stake among them, at $27.21 million. The bank held 712,319 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF, worth about $20.52 million, and it also opened a new position of 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF, worth about $6.7 million.

UBS and Morgan Stanley disclosed XRP fund holdings of $1.91 million and $116,000, respectively. Most of the UBS position was in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF, and Morgan Stanley held funds from Franklin, REX-Osprey and Bitwise.

JPMorgan Chase held 539 shares of the Bitwise fund, worth about $9,000, and National Bank of Canada held 330 shares of the same fund, worth about $5,500. Bank of Montreal held REX-Osprey and ProShares Ultra XRP shares worth $4,300.

The crypto portfolio of Goldman Sachs grew to $2.64 billion by the end of September, according to its 13F filing. The bank held about $1.28 billion in Bitcoin ETFs, and BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC accounted for $778 million and $398 million of that amount, respectively. Goldman also held about $1.22 billion in Ether funds, and BlackRock's ETHA accounted for $603 million of that amount.

Goldman held $144 million in XRP ETFs at the end of the third quarter, up from $87 million at the end of the second quarter. The bank's 13F filing for the first quarter showed no XRP or Solana ETF holdings, and Goldman still held no Solana funds at the end of September.

The bank held shares of five spot XRP funds from Franklin Templeton, Bitwise, Canary, Grayscale and 21Shares, and its Franklin Templeton position was worth almost $48 million.

Besides, trading firm Jane Street reported $23.5 million in XRP funds, and Simplex Trading disclosed a $14 million stake in the Grayscale fund. EP Wealth Advisors raised its Volatility Shares XRP ETF holding by 37% to 18,400 shares, worth about $148,000.

A 13F filing only shows long positions as of Sept. 30. It doesn't show whether the banks hedge those holdings with shorts, or what they did with the shares in October and November. Since then, XRP has fallen below $1, and on Tuesday morning, XRP was trading at $0.966.

#5128. Here’s how Ledger’s website was hit by the Optimizely malware attack

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the 16th of November, Ledger’s public website was infected with malware designed to swap crypto addresses and steal card details. Security researcher Scott Helme traced the code to Optimizely, a website testing provider. His team found compromised scripts tied to 178 organizations, including Ledger, the BBC, and Zoom.

In practice, the malware could swap a copied crypto address for one belonging to the attacker. So if a visitor pasted that address and approved the payment, their crypto could go to the attacker instead.

So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website. Whether it also affected Ledger’s hardware wallets or the Ledger Wallet app remains unclear.

Just over a month earlier, though, Ledger had faced a separate attack involving physical devices. In that case, Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold through a reseller contained unauthorized hardware.

At the time, AMBCrypto reported that the October theft had reached $91 million across more than 470 crypto addresses.

Report URI recorded the cleanup of Ledger’s script at 20:41 UTC that day. Early on the 17th of November, Optimizely said,

We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.

Report URI traced about $7,040 in crypto to addresses linked to the attack on the 16th of November. When Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn looked at where the money came from, he estimated that victims sent about $2,300. He said,

Most of the rest was the attacker’s own money. The attacker appears to have been very sloppy with their onchain hygiene

However, the number of Ledger visitors who lost funds remains unclear.

A similar breach had hit Polymarket a few weeks earlier. In that case, the malicious code could act on behalf of traders who were already signed in.

On the 29th of October, it sold some traders’ positions and moved funds out of their wallets.

Polymarket paused international trading to stop further losses. It later announced $3.9 million in reimbursements, including about $1.2 million for losses during the pause. By the 30th of October, the company said it had fully refunded 689 of the 726 affected wallets.

Japan’s Nikkei and South korea's KOSPI gain 1%, after Nvidia reports strong third-quarter revenue growth.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng falls 1.12% as its technology index hits four-month low.

U.S. restrictions on advanced AI chips add pressure to China’s technology stocks.

Nvidia’s record earnings gave Asia’s chip stocks another boost, but the rally did not reach every market. Japan’s Nikkei and South Korea’s KOSPI index posted strong gains.

In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index fell nearly 2 to hit a four-month low, as China tech stocks faced pressure from U.S. chip restrictions.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 index has climbed around 1% to trade over 59,334.28. The rally came after Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier.

SoftBank Group and Tokyo Electron each gained around 3%, while Trend Micro jumped 6%.

Meanwhile, South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index also gained around 0.79% to 5,079.54. Chipmakers led the rise, with SK Hynix up 4.19% and Samsung Electronics gaining 2.31%.

Nvidia added to the positive mood with its fourth-quarter revenue forecast of around $130 billion, giving semiconductor investors another reason to buy chip stocks.

Hong Kong is showing the other side of the AI trade. The Hang Seng Index fell 1.12% to 22,816.43, while the Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 2.5% to a four-month low.

Big tech stocks also came under heavy selling. Alibaba fell 2.63%, Tencent dropped 6.5%, Baidu declined 2.7%, while AI company MiniMax fell around 10%.

The pressure has grown after Washington expanded restrictions on advanced AI chip exports and remote access to high-end computing servers and overseas data centers.

Investors are also watching a meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping at APEC in Shenzhen. Technology and trade are expected to be key topics, especially as Shenzhen remains one of China’s major technology hubs.

Ahead of his meeting with Xi on November 19, Trump told APEC leaders that the U.S. opposes “any form of robust regulation” that could control or limit the development of superintelligence.

Beyond technology and trade, Trump also wants to discuss the wars in Ukraine and Iran. He could seek China’s help in pushing Russia toward peace.

#5126. Bitcoin's $90,000 Comeback Now Unlikely, Novogratz Warns

Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz said that the odds of Bitcoin hitting $90,000 by the end of 2026 are slim in light of prevailing macroeconomic headwinds and the growing likelihood that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates.

During a live event with Anthony Scaramucci at the Digital Assets Forum in New York City, Novogratz was asked if Bitcoin could get back to $90,000 by the end of this year.

"Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," Novogratz said.

His gloomy outlook comes as Bitcoin has struggled to rebound after a devastating drop that saw its price dip as low as $62,000 over the weekend. Bitcoin's price stood at around $64,600 on Nov. 17. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization has declined for six consecutive weeks.

A shift in the U.S. monetary policy outlook, namely the prospect of more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, has been largely to blame for Bitcoin's decline, according to Novogratz.

"At the start of the year, everybody thought the Fed was going to be cutting now," he said.

But high inflation and ongoing supply shocks have forced investors to readjust their expectations.

"Inflation's going up. We've got inflation going up," Novogratz said, warning that inflationary pressures could become increasingly entrenched.

"The Fed's going to hike. At least two more, probably three more," he said.

Novogratz predicted that the Fed would raise rates by 25 basis points in December and then hike again at its next meeting.

He said that higher rates, at least in the near term, tend to weigh on Bitcoin. But the higher cost of government borrowing could eventually provide support for the cryptocurrency.

"Yeah, later," he said in response to the suggestion that higher borrowing costs could be a tailwind for Bitcoin.

"First, you're gonna hike rates. Oh, sell gold, right? You're going to go to the dollar. It's so ingrained in peoples' heads," he said.

"Carry costs going up," he said. Bitcoin doesn't offer the same yield as interest-bearing dollar assets.

"You don't make any interest on Bitcoin in dollars," he said.

In particular, Novogratz said that the massive rise in Treasury yields has been particularly detrimental to the crypto market.

"Literally 40 basis points in like four days of trading. So that's why crypto's down," he said.

He also said that the massive crypto hack could still be weighing on investors' minds, adding to market jitters.

"I think in the back of their minds is the hack," he said.

The $62k-$63k area was a particularly dense STH supply cluster, and in recent days, there has been a positive reaction. The same area had been the base of the previous impulse move higher in mid-August.

If this area is breached, it could lead to another capitulation and new lows being formed.

Deeply negative apparent demand (30-day sum), with a 30-day reading of -247,700 BTC and a yearly measurement of -1.21 million BTC, highlighted severe market stress.

Crypto analyst Darkfost wrote that the metric, which is an indirect on-chain proxy based on new issuance versus changes in supply inactive for over a year, does not measure net cash outflows.

Nevertheless, it has historically been a reliable indicator that helps confirm trend strength. Right now, any price rebound without apparent demand easing toward neutral or positive levels would signal weakness.

#5124. BTC Price Drops 15% as Gold and Silver Dump: Can December’s Fed Decision Turn It?

BTC price fell 15% since Nov 5, more than gold and silver, as a December Fed hike nears 95% odds. Could this shift price action?

Gold (XAU) fell 2.5% to about $3,770 an ounce on Wednesday, November 18, as traders bet on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Silver dropped 3.3% to $45.70. Both metals are at their lowest since September 2025. The BTC price held near $64,600, but it has fallen even harder than the metals since the hike bets took off.

Gold prices sink beneath $3,800, hitting a 14-month low as the hawkish Fed outlook and firm dollar weigh on bullion – FX

— First Squawk (@FirstSquawk) November 18, 2026

We compared the moves since November 5, the day before a strong October jobs report changed the rate outlook. Bitcoin is down 15%, silver 12.5% and gold 8.4%. Over the same days, the U.S. dollar index rose 2.2%, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed from 4.84% to 5.10%.

Higher rates hit everything that pays no interest, and gold, silver and bitcoin all fall into that group. So the next big test is the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting.

Gold peaked near $5,320 an ounce on COMEX futures in late January. It has since lost 29%, and silver has lost 60% from its January high of $115. On Monday, gold for immediate delivery touched $3,832, and Wednesday’s drop pushed it lower still.

The reason is the Fed. Markets now treat another hike as almost certain:

A quarter-point hike would lift the Fed’s target range to 4.00%-4.25%. It would be the second this year, after September’s. Waller has gone further, saying a half-point move, or “a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered.”

Central banks are still buying gold, 675 tonnes in the first nine months of the year. That hasn’t been enough to offset a stronger dollar and higher yields.

#5123. Hoskinson: Cardano Not Done Yet

Charles Hoskinson made sure to clear up misunderstandings about whether he thought the work on Cardano was done.

"I never once said Cardano is finished," Hoskinson said in a Nov. 15 post on X.

The comments came after he talked about the completion of Cardano's original roadmap, which raised some questions about his role in the blockchain's future.

He also called out the CEO of the Cardano Foundation, Frederik Gregaard, for not mentioning the Midnight chain when discussing everything the network has accomplished.

In his latest video, uploaded on Nov. 17, Hoskinson celebrated the fact that Midnight had just brought on board its first UK-based banking partner, Monument Bank.

Monument Bank is the first UK bank to offer interest-bearing tokenized retail deposits on a public blockchain, according to an announcement from the Midnight Foundation.

Up to £250 million in customer deposits will be added to Midnight in the first phase, and each tokenized deposit will be backed 1:1 by sterling cash held at the bank.

Monument Bank customers can now earn a fixed 5.2% annual equivalent rate on deposits for 12 months, all without having to deal with cryptocurrencies directly.

Hoskinson was very excited about the scale of the initiative, comparing the planned amount of deposits with the current decentralized finance ecosystem on Cardano.

"It's five times the TVL of Cardano," he said.

The £250 million is the planned initial size of the banking product, not a verified figure for how much is currently deposited on Midnight.

Hoskinson called this one of the most important milestones in his career.

"This is just one of the many things to come, but I think it's one of the most significant things of at least my career," he said.

He added that the team behind Midnight had moved the originally scheduled hard fork from December to November to accommodate the technical needs of Monument Bank.

Despite the milestone, Hoskinson emphasized that it's only the first step in a much larger mission: bringing traditional financial assets onto Midnight.

Hoskinson thinks the main barrier to cryptocurrency adoption is the lack of trust among consumers. He believes that simplifying the user experience without compromising regulatory requirements will allow billions of people to join the blockchain economy.

Hoskinson also shared that there's a big event coming up for the Midnight Foundation on Dec. 15. Developers will showcase future products and technological advancements scheduled for 2027.

#5121. Anthropic IPO Price Could Top $80 And Pre-IPO Traders Are Copying the SpaceX Script: What Traders Should Expect

The Anthropic IPO may price above $80. Hyperliquid’s pre-IPO contract sits 24% higher, the setup SpaceX had before it listed.

The Anthropic IPO could price above $80 a share on Wednesday evening, above the $70 to $78 range the Claude AI maker set last week, The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. The newspaper cited stronger-than-expected investor demand. Its advisers have discussed a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion.

The shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, November 19, under the ticker ANT.

⚠️ What if $ANT mirrors $SPCX after the IPO? pic.twitter.com/pMd9aC7KQb

— Rand Group (@randgroup) November 18, 2026

Crypto traders have been betting on the Anthropic IPO for weeks. On Hyperliquid, a pre-IPO contract that tracks one ANT share trades near $99, about 23% above $80.

We have seen this setup before. The night before SpaceX listed in June, the same kind of contract traded 28% above its $135 IPO price. SpaceX then closed its first day 19% up, below what the contract had promised.

So what should traders know before the bell rings on Thursday?

Anthropic launched its roadshow, the week when a company pitches its shares to large investors, on November 10. Its announcement set the terms:

Demand has run ahead of that. Pricing above $80 would lift the valuation toward the $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion the advisers discussed. The final price is set after the US market closes on Wednesday, and the shares open on Thursday.

That price is what large investors pay in the Anthropic IPO. Most retail traders will buy at the opening price instead, which can be far higher.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Hyperliquid, a crypto exchange, lists contracts that let traders bet on a company’s share price before it lists. We compared its Anthropic contract with the one it ran for SpaceX, counting back from each listing day.

The SpaceX contract was right that the shares would jump, but too optimistic about how far. If Anthropic followed the same pattern, a 7% gap from Wednesday’s contract price would put ANT’s first close in the low $90s. That is a pattern from one listing, not a forecast.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Tumbles 19% Ahead of Anthropic IPO: Is SpaceX Crash Repeating?

On the hourly chart, Hyperliquid’s ANT contract trades at $98.83, down from $138 when it started trading on October 26.

The number to watch before the Anthropic IPO opens is tonight’s final price. Every dollar above $80 shrinks the contract’s 24% premium, and with it the room for the first-day pop that pre-IPO traders are betting on.

#5120. Analyst: XRP Below $1 Revives a 70% Bounce Bet

Home » Trendsetter News » Analyst: XRP Below $1 Revives a 70% Bounce Bet

XRP’s dip below $1 has revived hopes of a roughly 70% rebound, with one analyst citing a similar August rally.

XRP could repeat a roughly 70% rebound from below $1, according to a crypto commentator who points to an August rally as the template. In a new YouTube episode, Zach Rector argues that another sharp recovery is possible, though the case rests largely on a historical chart comparison rather than a confirmed catalyst.

The chart discussion puts XRP’s latest low near $0.89. The analyst says an earlier slide to $0.98 in August was followed by a rise toward $1.70 within four or five days.

“I’m not here to guarantee that that’s coming again,” Zach Rector says, before overlaying the earlier price pattern onto the latest decline. The analyst also suggests XRP could revisit $2 quickly, without committing to a date.

The explanation centers on leverage: the host argues that downside liquidations have largely cleared, leaving market makers an incentive to drive prices higher. The transcript provides no liquidation figures, order-book data or positioning metrics to substantiate that view.

That distinction matters. A previous bounce illustrates how sharply XRP can recover, but it does not establish that selling pressure is exhausted or rule out another decline.

The more consequential adoption discussion concerns the analyst’s claim that 1,700 institutions, corporations and enterprises use Ripple solutions. Rector explicitly acknowledges that there is no breakdown showing how many use products involving XRP.

Zach Rector also defends Ripple’s emphasis on its RLUSD stablecoin, arguing that greater stablecoin liquidity could attract activity to the XRP Ledger.

A statement attributed to Old Glory Bank supports offering both XRP and stablecoins, with regulated stablecoins potentially better suited to payments where businesses require certainty of value.

Still, stablecoin issuance on the ledger should not be confused with evidence that every payment requires XRP as an intermediary. The YouTube video does not establish that connection, despite the host’s bullish interpretation.

Zach Rector also identifies a proposed lending protocol as a potential source of collateral demand.

For crypto enthusiasts, these are separate propositions to track: a short-term rebound based on chart resemblance, and a longer-term investment case that depends on measurable network activity, liquidity and actual XRP usage.
