#5081. What is Ethereum actually for? A judge and Vitalik Buterin both left it open

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit. This judgement came about after the government failed to prove the brothers made any “material misrepresentation.”

The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

On a similar note, Ethereum [ETH] co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued that digital assets do not match up to investing in houses. These three developments, when taken together, compound the question of what crypto is actually for.

On the 2nd of April 2023, the brothers seemingly exploited a bug in the MEV-Boost relay software, due to which they could view transactions that sandwich traders believed were private.

The brothers’ alleged proposal for replacement transactions, in turn, resulted in massive losses of roughly $25 million within seconds.

Finally, on the 16th of November 2026, Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke, when granting an acquittal, wrote,

The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos’ conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.

It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case. Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted.

The court analyzed the government’s theories – including the “lure transactions” and the so-called “false signature,” and found nothing that could support a wire fraud conviction.

A couple of days later, on the 18th of November, Horsley posted on X:

Rolling bank outages in the AI era – Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.

The post came as thousands of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo customers reported being unable to access their accounts.

Vitalik Buterin, in a separate post on November 18, argued that younger generations have been investing in digital assets over real estate options; doing so, he noted, reduces –

Perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive.

But he added a condition: housing had the advantage of being –

A culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.

Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior… We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The three developments have been framing crypto’s developing role separately, but these assets have a long way to go before they can fully replace TradFi.

Vitalik Buterin himself leaves the question open, as he observed,

We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The ruling did not answer that question, nor did the outage.

DUBAI, UAE, November 18, 2026 – WSDT is introducing its prop trading platform for cryptocurrency perpetual futures, gold and tokenized US stocks. Traders can access these markets through a single simulated account, with one-step evaluations starting at a one-time fee of $19 for a $1,500 account.

The platform combines crypto perpetual futures, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, with xStocks instruments tracking companies such as Apple, NVIDIA and Tesla, alongside stock-index ETFs. Perpetual futures are contracts without an expiry date; xStocks track the prices of underlying shares or ETFs. On WSDT, these instruments are traded in a simulated environment, without ownership of the underlying shares or tokens.

Positions across the markets share the same account balance and count toward the same evaluation. Traders can work across crypto and equity-linked instruments in one terminal while managing a single set of account limits.

A WSDT challenge tests trading performance against a 10% profit target, a 4% daily loss limit and a 6% maximum drawdown fixed against the starting account size. Traders must trade on at least four separate days, with no deadline to complete the evaluation. Account sizes range from $1,500 to $200,000, with fees varying by size.

Traders who pass move to a funded-stage account, which is also simulated and retains the loss limits. They receive 80% of eligible profits under WSDT’s Provider Service Agreement. The evaluation fee pays for access to the challenge; it is not a trading deposit.

Registered users can open a free 14-day demo with a $100,000 simulated balance, without providing a payment card or making a deposit. The demo uses the same terminal as challenges, allowing traders to practice before entering an evaluation. Demo results do not qualify for payouts.

WSDT also runs an ongoing weekly competition with free entry. Every participant starts with a $240,000 simulated balance, and the top three finishers receive challenge accounts. A new round opens each Monday at noon New York time. Winners must pass their awarded challenge before progressing to the funded stage.

Registration, account options and full challenge rules are available on the WSDT website.

WSDT provides trader evaluation and educational services across crypto, gold and tokenized equity instruments. Built by TEFS, a prop trading firm established in 2017, it is operated by TEFS Marketing Management L.L.C. in Dubai, UAE. All WSDT trading accounts are simulated.

#5078. Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

Alibaba released Qwen 4 Max on Monday, its most powerful AI model yet and the first flagship built on its new Qwen 4 architecture.

It is also the highest-ranked Chinese model on Arena's agent leaderboard, putting the company ahead of Tencent, Moonshot AI and DeepSeek in that particular test.

The new model has 2.4 trillion parameters, can process text, images and video, and accepts up to one million tokens of context. Parameters are all the different dials a model can handle and tweak when processing information. Tokens are basically the smallest unit of information a model can handle. Its current configuration is enough room for lengthy codebases or stacks of documents.

Alibaba uses a mixture-of-experts design, which keeps most of those parameters idle for any given word it processes. Qwen 4 Max activates 71 billion at a time, compared with 95 billion for Qwen 3.8 Max, allowing a very large model to use less computing power per token.

On Agent Arena, Qwen 4 Max placed 14th among individual models and made Alibaba the fifth-ranked laboratory overall.

The leaderboard evaluates real agent sessions using task completion, user satisfaction and how well models respond to corrections, then scores each model by its net percentage improvement over an average competitor. Qwen 4 Max posted a preliminary 7.46% score across 14,727 sessions, the highest among Chinese entries.

Its visual work may be the more interesting part for regular users. The Code Arena web-development ranking compares websites built by AI models using head-to-head user votes and a points-based rating system. Qwen 4 Max debuted sixth globally at 1,750 points, up 74 from its predecessor, and placed eighth in categories for branding and reference-based design.

That puts it in the same neighborhood as the best American models at turning a request, a screenshot or a rough idea into a working interface that actually looks good.

Alibaba's demos go further, showing the model building game environments and translating factory layouts into 3D models, although those are company-selected examples rather than independent tests.

The visual capability is for understanding images and video and producing code or other text-based outputs. It is not the same as releasing a new image generator.

Qwen 4 Max costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million generated tokens through QwenCloud, a 25% reduction from the previous flagship's $2 and $6 rates. Reused input served from an automatic cache costs $0.075 per million tokens, which can make repetitive workflows substantially cheaper.

Alibaba says its internal testing across hundreds of professional specialties found that the model used 35% fewer tokens and reduced average task costs by roughly 60% compared with Qwen 3.8 Max. In other words, it should be cheaper to execute tasks on this model even against competitors with a similar price..

The bigger limitation for the community is that Qwen 4 Max is closed-weight. Developers can use it through an API or Alibaba's apps, but they cannot download its internal parameters, modify it or run it privately on their own hardware.

Qwen has become a foundation for the open-model ecosystem. An August report from Hugging Face counted 151,448 Qwen-based derivative models on its platform, about 4.7 times the number built specifically on Meta's Llama family. Those include community fine-tunes and optimized versions that power local assistants and specialized tools.

Alibaba opened the weights of Qwen 3.8 Max earlier this year, despite having kept some previous Max models proprietary. It also previewed elements of the Qwen 4 architecture with smaller models months before Monday's release.

The launch lands in a crowded Chinese race. Moonshot's Kimi K3 pushed enormous open-weight models toward Western performance, while DeepSeek has been competing hard on API prices.

Qwen 4 Max leads some Chinese rankings, but American labs still hold the top spots in Arena's overall agent and web-development tables. They are also considerably more expensive.

Alibaba says smaller Qwen 4 models will be released with open weights, giving developers a chance to build on this generation rather than simply rent its biggest model. It has not announced their sizes or release dates.

#5077. How did Coinbase stop deepfake Elon Musk’s promise to double your crypto?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Scammers recently used a fake video of Elon Musk to get people to send them crypto. It didn’t go to plan.

Especially since according to Coinbase, it blocked a big chunk of those transfers before the money could disappear.

… and Coinbase stopped $4.7 million from reaching scammers.

Someone put out a YouTube livestream made to look like a Tesla flying car demo. On screen was an AI-made Elon Musk, and the pitch was to send crypto and get 2x back.

More than half a million people tuned in. The stream flashed wallet addresses and QR codes. So, sending money took just a scan.

In a blog post, Coinbase laid out what happened. In about two hours, hundreds of its users tried to send funds to the scammers. Its automated fraud system caught about 91% of that.

The real Musk had nothing to do with any of it.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that Coinbase hasn’t said how much of the remaining 9% actually got through.

Its fraud agent watches outgoing transfers as they happen.

If any transfer looks off or iffy, like a payment to a freshly created wallet or something tied to a “giveaway,” the agent in question steps in. In such a case, the agent opens a chat with the user, explains why the transfer might be risky, and prompts them to think twice before proceeding.

It even checks its own replies before showing them. According to Coinbase, no person was involved at any point. Nobody’s account got hacked either. No passwords leaked. People (some of them long-time users) chose to hit send because the fake Musk was convincing.

Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent.

That is exactly what makes these scams tough.

It isn’t the first fake Elon Musk either. A doctored video in 2023 reportedly cost victims around $160K. In June 2024, deepfake giveaways popped up on more than 35 YouTube channels during a Starship launch.

The Single Asset Vault amendment on the XRP Ledger is getting closer to activation on the mainnet as validator support builds for the network’s preparation to enable better DeFi functionality.

According to data from XRPScan, the SingleAssetVault amendment, or XLS-65, has received yes votes from 25 of 35 trusted validators, currently standing at 71.43% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of 35 votes (29) to start its 14-day countdown to activation. That means it needs four more votes to get there and could reach the magic number before the end of 2026.

The XRP Ledger’s amendment process requires a proposed amendment to be approved by more than 80% of trusted validators for 14 days before it is implemented. Validator support may shift during this time, and if the required 80% threshold is lost, activation may be delayed.

The Single Asset Vault amendment creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. The amendment introduces a Vault object that defines the state of a tokenized vault, and the Vault entry is one of the ledger entry types it provides.

The Vault object holds important information such as available assets, shares, total value, and other relevant information. Users can create a Vault object with the VaultCreate transaction; the Vault object is tracked in an Owner Directory owned by the Vault Owner account.

The XRP Ledger lending amendment has gained additional yes votes. According to XRPScan, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, also known as XLS-66, has received 24 yes votes out of 35 trusted validators, meaning it has 68.57% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of the 35 votes (29) to trigger a 14-day activation countdown.

This implies that there are five votes left for it to reach this threshold, with the possibility of it securing the required number of votes before the end of 2026 as well.

According to XRP enthusiasts, LendingProtocolV1_1 represents the biggest amendment for unlocking capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger and is anticipated by institutional and retail users.

#5075. Google Warns North Korean Hackers Are Poisoning AI Tools to Drain Crypto Firms

Home » Crypto Market News » Google Warns North Korean Hackers Are Poisoning AI Tools to Drain Crypto Firms

State-backed hackers are using fake recruiters and tampered Claude Code settings to breach crypto networks.

Cyberattacks against the cryptocurrency industry have crossed a dangerous threshold as threat actors shift from basic AI prompts to autonomous AI agents capable of running intrusions from start to finish.

According to the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant report, state-backed hackers are actively targeting crypto firms in North America and Europe by turning popular AI developer tools into malware delivery traps.

Researchers have linked a suspected North Korean hacking campaign to attacks on cryptocurrency companies. The group, known as Midnight Neptune, uses fake recruiter profiles and tampered software settings to break into company networks.

The attackers approach targets on professional networking platforms, posing as recruiters with AI-generated profile photos.

They then invite victims to fake online meetings, where simulated audio or video problems prompt them to run scripts to fix the issue. This social engineering trick, known as ClickFix, gets victims to execute malicious commands themselves.

Once inside a company’s network, the attackers tamper with its internal code repositories, modifying the configuration file used by Anthropic’s Claude Code.

The next time a developer launches Claude Code, the altered settings silently download a backdoor called SOMBERMEME.

The attackers also create GitHub Personal Access Tokens disguised as Microsoft Copilot to make their activity look like normal developer traffic.

The report also revealed a major advance in automated hacking that puts open-source Web3 infrastructure at risk.

Google researchers discovered an active tool called exploit_agent on an exposed testing server. It uses large language models (LLMs) to compare software code before and after security updates, identify newly patched vulnerabilities, write code to exploit them, and launch attacks — all without human involvement.

That puts open-source protocols at risk. Since code updates are publicly available, hackers can spot newly fixed vulnerabilities and exploit them before operators have a chance to install the patches. Even a brief delay can leave networks vulnerable.

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported that disclosed vulnerabilities and exploits nearly doubled between January and August 2026.

Exploited zero-day vulnerabilities also rose from an average of eight per month in 2025 to 11 in 2026, reaching 22 in August alone.

Beyond traditional cyberattacks, Mandiant warns of a growing threat called LLMJacking. Criminals hijack corporate cloud accounts, steal AI computing power, and resell it through underground marketplaces known as LLM Mixers. The resulting fraud can exceed $100,000 in a single day and reach $1 million per victim.

Meanwhile, influence networks use more than 100,000 fake social media accounts to spread misinformation, fuel token hype, and trigger artificial market panic.

To counter these threats, Google is deploying AI security tools such as Big Sleep and CodeMender to find and fix software vulnerabilities before hackers exploit them.

The GTIG report highlights several security risks for the crypto industry.

Companies using AI coding tools should check their code repositories for unauthorized commands and keep third-party access tokens secure.

They also need to install software updates quickly, as AI-powered hackers can turn newly discovered vulnerabilities into working attacks.

Employees should never follow unexpected browser or video-call instructions asking them to copy and run computer commands.

Investors, meanwhile, should be cautious of sudden waves of online hype or panic, which fake social media accounts can create at scale.

#5073. What will OpenAI’s new outside safety evaluator tell the public?

Under a four-month pilot, Apollo Research can flag access gaps and explain how redactions affect what the public can verify.

OpenAI is bringing in Apollo Research, an outside AI safety group, for a four-month investigation into whether OpenAI’s models try to bypass safeguards. Apollo can disclose any limits OpenAI places on its access to evidence. OpenAI can redact confidential supporting evidence from the public reports, and Apollo can explain how any redactions affect its conclusions. The agreement protects Apollo’s verdict on each claim from redaction.

Six Apollo evaluators will work inside OpenAI. They will examine whether training encourages models to undermine safeguards, whether safety tests can draw out that behavior, whether it happens during internal use, and whether evaluators can detect the reasoning behind it.

OpenAI confirmed the engagement on November 16 as part of a first phase involving four outside assessors. OpenAI says Apollo is paid for its work and that compensation does not depend on the assessment’s results.

For the training inquiry, Apollo says it will have access to relevant code and datasets and be able to query intermediate training checkpoints. It will also get relevant reinforcement-learning records, including rewards and available reasoning traces. Access details for the other three inquiries were still to be agreed when Apollo announced the pilot on November 16.

The review covers agreed claims, models and time periods. OpenAI can withhold even in-scope material when it considers that reasonably necessary because of technical limits, security risks or intellectual property protection. It must tell Apollo that material was withheld and give written reasons. Where OpenAI considers it feasible and relevant, it will also identify the categories and approximate volume of withheld records. Unfavorable information alone cannot justify withholding access.

Apollo plans two public reports. The first will address whether training encouraged models to undermine safeguards. The second will cover safety testing, internal use and whether the reasoning behind such behavior can be detected. OpenAI can review the reports for confidential material, and its commitments bar it from requesting a redaction solely because a finding is unfavorable. The Safety and Security Committee of the OpenAI Foundation’s board will receive unredacted copies.

The agreement also covers what Apollo learns from employees. OpenAI selects who can discuss confidential information, and formal interviews are logged. The conversations are off the record. To publish a claim arising from an interview, Apollo must establish it independently or obtain a formal attestation from OpenAI.

If OpenAI declines to attest, Apollo can say so publicly and explain the effect on its conclusions while keeping the underlying information confidential.

Apollo can publicly describe the access it requested and received, any limits or delays OpenAI imposed, and the reasons the company gave. It can also discuss the terms of the pilot without first submitting those comments to OpenAI for review.

#5071. Solana Foundation Backs CoinGecko as Crypto Data Giant Eyes Trading

Solana Foundation Backs CoinGecko as Crypto Data Giant Eyes Trading

CoinGecko, one of crypto’s most widely used price-tracking sites, wants to do more than show users where markets are heading.

The crypto data platform said Tuesday that it has received backing from the Solana Foundation, the Switzerland-based nonprofit that supports the Solana network, to speed its expansion into market intelligence, new digital asset products and, potentially, trading.

The announcement came on the final day of Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London.

The Solana Foundation did not specify the size of the commitment, but a representative for the foundation told Decrypt it is taking a majority stake in CoinGecko. The terms were not disclosed.

CoinGecko said it will focus on three areas: expanding data coverage and analytics across blockchain ecosystems, exploring trading features that let users act onchain, and building simpler experiences for users worldwide.

“We’ve helped millions of people discover and understand this industry, but the opportunity ahead is much bigger,” said Bobby Ong, CoinGecko’s CEO and co-founder.

Vibhu Norby, chief product officer at the Solana Foundation, said the foundation believes the “next wave of adoption will come from making crypto dramatically easier to use.” (Disclosure: Decrypt’s parent company, Dastan, is building products on Solana, and Decrypt uses CoinGecko market data.)

Founded in 2014, CoinGecko says it provides data on more than 50 million crypto assets across more than 2,000 exchanges.

CoinGecko said it will keep serving users with the same commitment to “reliable, comprehensive market coverage and transparent methodologies.” Co-founder and President TM Lee said its commitment to accurate, reliable data “remains unchanged.”

The deal is one of several Solana announcements timed around Breakpoint. DTCC said last week that it plans to connect its tokenization service to Solana, with tokenized stocks, ETFs and Treasuries expected on the network in the second half of 2027.

At a Breakpoint panel, executives from DTCC and Barclays said tokenization’s biggest near-term payoff lies in putting idle collateral to work.

Asset manager Bitwise has filed an S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash (ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The document appeared in the SEC's database on Nov. 17, 2026. On Wednesday, ZEC rose to $975 before it pulled back to around $927.

Zcash is often called a "more secret" version of Bitcoin. According to the S-1, the Zcash network supports two types of transactions, and the "shielded" ones use a form of zero-knowledge cryptography known as zk-SNARKs. Holders of shielded Zcash "may selectively disclose transaction information to third parties," the filing says.

Bitwise's fund will not use this feature. "The Trust does not engage in shielded transactions in connection with its activities," according to the document.

The shares are expected to list on the Dallas-based Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) under the ticker ZEC. According to the S-1, Coinbase Custody Trust Company will act as the Zcash custodian, and BNY Mellon will serve as the cash custodian. Bitwise also wrote that "the Trust will not stake or otherwise seek to derive additional Zcash from its holdings." The sponsor fee in the filing is listed as "0.___% per annum."

In the risk section of the S-1, Bitwise wrote that "a number of digital asset trading platforms have delisted Zcash, restricted trading in Zcash or declined to support Zcash." According to the filing, many of these platforms cited regulatory or compliance concerns.

The platforms that still support Zcash "do so only with respect to transparent addresses and do not permit deposits or withdrawals to or from shielded addresses," the document says. Bitwise also pointed to new EU rules that take effect on July 10, 2027. According to the S-1, the rules will "prohibit credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers in the European Union" from keeping accounts in such assets.

Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan named Zcash one of his top three assets for the decade in September, alongside Bitcoin and tokenization projects. Three days before the S-1 filing, he called ZEC a "golden mean" between open Bitcoin and anonymous Monero in an interview.

Grayscale's Zcash fund (ZCSH) has traded on NYSE Arca since August 2026, and the Winklevoss brothers filed for their own Zcash ETF on Nasdaq in October. ZCSH held $496.79 million as of the Nov. 17 close, according to SoSoValue. The fund has attracted $168.76 million in net inflows since its launch, and it recorded no inflows on Nov. 17, when Bitwise filed its S-1.

Home » Exchanges » Revolut Lists GoMining Token for UK and European Users

The move brings the niche utility token to more than 15 million fintech app users under the EU’s MiCA regulatory framework.

Retail fintech giant Revolut has added GOMINING, the native utility token of the digital Bitcoin mining platform GoMining, to its in-app cryptocurrency trading service. The listing enables over 15 million Revolut crypto users across the United Kingdom and the European Economic Area (EEA) to buy, hold, and trade the token alongside everyday banking services.

Prior to this integration, GOMINING was primarily accessible through crypto-native exchanges such as Kraken, KuCoin, and Bitget.

The listing builds on an existing payment integration established in 2024 that allowed European users to fund GoMining accounts via Revolut Pay. It also adds GOMINING to Revolut’s cryptocurrency trading service.

Revolut reviews digital assets before listing them, assessing their risks, compliance requirements and potential financial crime exposure. It also monitors listed tokens on an ongoing basis as part of its procedures under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

“For years, there has been a clear line between crypto and traditional finance, and most people stayed on one side of it,” said Mark Zalan, CEO of GoMining, in a statement announcing the listing. “For GoMining, this listing means our token is no longer only for people who already live in the crypto world.”

GOMINING has several uses within the GoMining platform. Token holders can use it to pay digital miner maintenance fees, with discounts of up to 20%, buy digital miners on the platform’s marketplace and purchase boosts in Miner Wars, GoMining’s mining game.

The token also has a governance function. Users can lock their GOMINING tokens to receive veGOMINING, which gives them voting rights on the allocation of ecosystem rewards.

Revolut customers can now buy GOMINING directly through the app. To use the token on GoMining, they must first transfer it to an external GoMining account.

The Revolut listing gives GOMINING exposure to a wider retail audience through a mainstream financial app. It also provides another way for users to acquire the token without first opening an account on a crypto-native exchange.

However, buying GOMINING through Revolut does not provide direct access to GoMining’s platform features. Users must transfer their tokens to an external wallet before using them within the GoMining ecosystem.

#5067. Backpack’s US approval could threaten offshore exchanges’ grip on crypto futures trading

The exchange plans to bring American and international traders into one regulated marketplace, potentially shifting liquidity and price discovery toward the US.

Crypto exchange Backpack has secured US regulatory approval to launch a futures exchange aimed at uniting American and international trading liquidity.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) designated Backpack's TLD Markets as a regulated futures exchange on Nov. 16, three days after approving its affiliated clearinghouse, TLD Clearing.

The approvals establish the regulatory foundation for Backpack to offer leveraged crypto perpetual futures to American traders while connecting them to the company's international trading operations.

However, Backpack's ambitions extend beyond entering the American derivatives market. The company wants to consolidate its global trading business under a single US-regulated exchange, eliminating the separation between domestic and overseas customers.

“There will be no Backpack international vs Backpack USA. Our entire platform will be operating on our CFTC regulated venue.”

The move represents a significant shift for a company that began in Chicago nearly four years ago before expanding its operations overseas.

Ferrante recalled that Backpack was “forced offshore” early in its development, prompting the company to establish operations across international markets while pursuing regulatory approval.

He described the CFTC approval as the culmination of nearly four years of work to return to the United States.

The proposed structure could reshape how American traders access cryptocurrency derivatives, particularly perpetual futures, which allow investors to maintain leveraged positions without a fixed expiration date.

Historically, regulatory restrictions have separated American crypto derivatives markets from much of the trading activity concentrated on offshore exchanges.

This fragmentation can limit available liquidity, widen the difference between buying and selling prices, and increase the cost of executing large transactions.

Backpack wants to address this by bringing eligible American and international traders into a shared order book, allowing their buy and sell orders to interact within the same regulated marketplace.

Under such an arrangement, an American trader seeking to purchase Bitcoin perpetual futures could potentially execute against sell orders submitted by overseas participants.

A larger pool of competing orders could improve market depth, narrow spreads and reduce the price impact of substantial trades.

Backpack US President Mark Wetjen said the initiative could help shift “price discovery from offshore unregulated venues to the United States.”

The company also plans to offer round-the-clock trading, support fiat and cryptocurrency collateral, and introduce cross-margining, allowing eligible positions to share available collateral.

The exchange will operate through TLD Markets, while its US-registered clearinghouse, TLD Clearing, will handle qualifying transactions.

Backpack's international reach provides an existing business to support this ambition. The company says it serves customers across more than 150 countries and regions and has processed over $450 billion in trading volume.

However, the extent to which that activity will move onto the US-regulated platform remains unclear.

Backpack has not disclosed its initial perpetual futures contracts, which overseas participants will be eligible to access the unified order book, or when trading will begin. Its US website is also currently accepting waitlist registrations.

XRP Ledger (XRPL) has marked a significant step in its journey to institutional adoption by becoming the first public permissionless layer-1 blockchain to see its principles of Architecture and Resiliency independently verified by the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

The independent attestation report was released on Nov. 13, further strengthening the assertion of XRP Ledger's compliance with institutional financial infrastructure requirements.

The Global Layer One initiative is a collaborative effort between prominent financial institutions and policymakers to set standards for digital financial infrastructure.

Its main goal is to make cross-border transactions for tokenised assets seamless while ensuring that blockchain networks adhere to internationally expected standards for financial market infrastructure.

Interestingly, XRPLF self-assessed XRPL for all 10 principles.

CertiK independently verified it only for the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

XRPLF also provided details on how requirements specific to private/permissioned networks are addressed by managing related risks for XRPL’s decentralized nature, open-source governance model, and protocol amendments.

It does not mean that XRPL meets all the standards mentioned in the toolkit completely.

Nonetheless, it's another step towards XRPL's bid to be a possible infrastructure for regulated financial institutions looking for blockchain-based settlement and tokenization.

#5065. Judge Acquits MIT Brothers in $25M Ethereum MEV Case, Ending Prosecution

Judge Acquits MIT Brothers in $25M Ethereum MEV Case, Ending Prosecution

A federal judge in Manhattan has acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, the MIT-educated brothers accused of exploiting Ethereum's transaction ordering system to take $25 million from automated trading bots.

U.S. District Judge Jessica Clarke granted the brothers' motion for a judgment of acquittal on Monday, clearing them of wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering, according to her ruling. The decision closes the criminal case without a second trial.

"The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes," Clarke wrote. To convict on wire fraud, prosecutors had to show the brothers made a material misrepresentation, and none of the government's theories did so, she found. Ethereum, she noted, is a "trustless, highly adversarial environment with no terms of use."

While the brothers' scheme "may have frustrated the spirit" of MEV-Boost, software that lets Ethereum validators outsource the ordering of transactions to specialized block builders, that was not enough to make out fraud, Clarke said. In a footnote, she added that the prosecution "raises serious due process concerns," though she declined to rule on that question.

Because the money laundering charge relied on the proceeds of the alleged wire fraud, it fell with the fraud counts.

The case stemmed from an April 2023 exploit targeting so-called sandwich bots, automated traders that profit from maximal extractable value (MEV) by placing their own trades on either side of other users' transactions.

According to the ruling, the brothers placed bait transactions designed to lure specific bots, then exploited a bug in a relay's code to see the bots' bundled trades before committing to a block. They then swapped the bait transactions for trades that sold the tokens instead, leaving the bots with about $25 million in losses in roughly 12 seconds. Authorities arrested the pair in May 2024, saying they spent months planning the attack and took steps to hide the proceeds.

At trial in Manhattan last year, an insider testified that the brothers had allegedly planned the attack, and the defense had earlier sought to block evidence of their Google searches. Clarke declared a mistrial in November 2025, after the jury deadlocked.

The case was closely watched in the crypto industry. Clarke's ruling described it as a "first of its kind" prosecution, a label the government itself used in its indictment.

The Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on Nov. 18 with seven recommendations on the draft documents CP26/36 and GC26/7. Three of them concern CP26/36, and four concern GC26/7. The letter was signed by HPC chief executive Jake Chervinsky.

The UK's new crypto regime will start to apply on Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA opened its window for crypto license applications on Sept. 30, 2026, and the window will close on Feb. 28, 2027.

According to the letter, "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity." HPC argued that attaching obligations to a person who could not discharge them "would offer consumers no additional protection."

In the letter, HPC also compared public blockchains with the internet. "Like a public blockchain, the internet depends on protocols that identifiable persons maintain and upgrade over time," the group wrote.

HPC asked the FCA to assess each participant in a blockchain network separately. Proprietary traders and market makers "supply much of the liquidity on which order books depend," the group wrote. HPC also asked the regulator to describe compliance requirements as outcomes and to hold regulated firms accountable for them.

On Aug. 24, HPC urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to harmonize their rules for perpetual contracts. The group argued that such products should be classified by their economic structure. According to HPC, a harmonized framework would let exchanges compete on "execution quality and liquidity."

On Sept. 30, HPC sent its response to the European Union's review of the MiCA rules. In it, the group asked the EU to treat crypto perpetual futures as derivatives under MiFID II. "Clarity in application, rather than new legislation, is what would assist in regulating perpetual futures," HPC wrote at the time.

Chervinsky previously served as chief policy officer at the Blockchain Association and as chief legal officer at the crypto venture firm Variant.

#5063. Germany moves to freeze Bitcoin for up to 180 days, even without access to private keys

The Bundestag-approved bill would let customs legally restrict suspicious crypto holdings in self-custody wallets, but enforcement poses a challenge authorities have yet to resolve.

Germany's parliament has approved legislation allowing customs authorities to freeze suspicious crypto holdings, including assets stored in self-custody wallets.

The Bundestag passed the bill on Nov. 12, advancing a broader government effort to combat money laundering and financial crime by expanding authorities' powers to investigate assets of questionable origin.

Under the proposed legislation, German customs could temporarily freeze significant assets, including cryptocurrencies, when factual evidence raises doubts about their lawful origin.

The approved committee text identifies assets worth more than €100,000 as a general benchmark for significant holdings. Authorities could also combine closely connected assets when determining whether they qualify.

Customs would initially have 30 days to investigate suspicious holdings, with a finance court authorized to extend the restriction by another 150 days if investigators demonstrate credible doubts about their origin and grounds for further investigation.

The legislation, however, has not completed its final approval process. As of Nov. 18, final consideration by the Bundesrat, Germany's chamber representing the states, and publication in the Federal Law Gazette remained outstanding.

The proposed rules could have different consequences depending on whether investors hold their Bitcoin through centralized exchanges or control their wallets directly.

For assets held on an exchange, German authorities could issue an enforceable attachment order requiring the custodian to restrict withdrawals from an affected account.

The mechanism draws on Germany's existing tax enforcement provisions, which allow authorities to prevent third parties from releasing assets subject to a legally enforceable attachment.

However, enforcing similar restrictions against self-custody wallets presents a more complicated challenge.

Unlike centralized exchanges, self-custody wallets allow users to control the private keys needed to authorize Bitcoin transactions without relying on a financial intermediary.

Germany's proposed framework addresses such holdings by treating cryptocurrencies as attachable property rights.

Under Section 321 of the German Fiscal Code, authorities can attach certain property rights without involving a third party by serving the holder with a legal prohibition on disposing of them.

Applied to eligible self-custodied Bitcoin, this could prohibit an owner from transferring the affected assets without automatically removing their ability to authorize blockchain transactions.

Consequently, an individual could remain technically capable of moving Bitcoin despite being legally prohibited from doing so.

Two ways a customs attachment could reach bitcoin, depending on who controls the transfers.

An order can restrict disposal even when the holder still controls the keys.

Illustrative cases under the Bundestag-approved bill. The diagram covers the effect of serving the attachment order.

Germany's Blockchain Bundesverband highlighted this enforcement challenge in a submission on an earlier version of the legislation. The industry association explained that authorities must distinguish between cryptocurrencies held by custodians and assets controlled directly by individuals.

It also warned that identifying a blockchain wallet does not necessarily establish who controls its assets, particularly where multiple parties share transaction-signing authority.

These complications could make enforcing restrictions on self-custody wallets harder than freezing balances held by regulated exchanges.

The legislation also distinguishes temporary asset freezes from permanent confiscation, which would require a separate finance court decision establishing that the property originated unlawfully.

Should the bill complete Germany's legislative process, its effectiveness against self-custodied crypto holdings will depend on authorities' ability to identify wallet controllers and enforce legal restrictions without direct control of their private keys.

Nvidia Board Not Considering Jensen Huang's Return: Report

Nvidia's board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, despite a growing campaign for his return led by some of the biggest names in tech and backed by President Donald Trump.

The board is focused on its investigation into Huang and is not in discussions to reinstate him, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday. Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, after 33 years at the helm of the company he co-founded. His departure followed his admission of an affair and reports that he had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at an Nvidia customer whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, as well as with Nvidia employees. The week of revelations saw hundreds of billions of dollars wiped from Nvidia's market value.

The report cuts against a weekend of growing pressure for Huang's return. The Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed a comeback with allies, though Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner, one of the investors urging the board to keep "all options" open, told CNBC that Huang had not discussed returning with him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on the speculation.

An online petition calling for Huang's reinstatement had drawn 191,996 signatures by Monday. Its backers include Elon Musk, who said on Friday that he was signing it, as well as Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The site notes that signatories' affiliations are self-reported and unverified. Nvidia employees have also pushed internally for his return.

Trump said on Monday that he would welcome Huang back. "I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters, adding that national security had not been put at risk, as Decrypt reported. That puts him at odds with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who said on Sunday that Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO.

Others in tech have stopped short of backing a return. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who was briefly ousted from his own company in 2023, said at a Semafor conference on Monday that Huang had "long been a hero of mine," but that he did not know enough to say whether Huang should come back.

Nvidia shares closed down 4.1% at $156.14 on Monday, and were down a further 0.5% at $155.67 in premarket trading early on Tuesday, according to Yahoo! Finance data.

Nvidia's board said on Friday that it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, the interim CEO, will lead the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday.

#5059. Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam

Coinbase (COIN) said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million in customer funds from reaching scammers who used a deepfake of Elon Musk to pitch a fake Tesla crypto giveaway, blocking roughly 91% of the money customers tried to send. The exchange described the incident in a Tuesday blog post, part of a weekly series on consumer protection. It said the system worked “with no humans in the loop.”

Those two figures imply customers tried to send about $5.2 million, and that roughly $460,000 still left their accounts. Coinbase did not say how much reached the scammers.

The scam ran during Tesla’s “flying car” demo. Scammers set up a YouTube livestream that looked like the real broadcast, with a deepfake Musk, on-screen wallet addresses and a QR code. The stream promised to double any crypto sent to it, and more than half a million people watched, Coinbase said.

Over about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the addresses on screen. Many were long-time users. Coinbase did not say when the fake stream ran or which coins customers tried to send.

The company stressed that its platform was not breached. “Nobody was hacked,” Coinbase wrote. “No Coinbase account was broken into, no password stolen, no credential phished.” That is what makes giveaway fraud hard to stop, since most defenses look for activity the account holder did not authorize, and here the customers logged in and pressed confirm themselves.

“Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent,” the post said.

Coinbase said its defense has three parts. Machine learning models first score outgoing sends in real time, watching for giveaway patterns, brand impersonation and newly created wallet addresses. The goal, the company wrote, is “to catch the danger, not the customer.” When a send is flagged, a scam-specific agent takes over, looking up context, naming the scam pattern, explaining how giveaway schemes work and asking questions meant to make the story fall apart.

Each reply is scored for confidence before the customer sees it, so the system knows when a situation needs more friction. The agent had never been trained on this kind of con, Coinbase said. Deepfake giveaways tied to a live product launch were not in its training data.

“It recognized the shape of the scheme anyway,” the company wrote, pointing to the promise to multiply funds, the deadline of a live event and a transfer that could not be reversed.

Coinbase said deepfakes have changed the economics of the scam. Staging something like this once took “a crew, a studio, and weeks,” it wrote. “Now it takes a livestream slot and a model.” The company said it is expanding AI review of risky sends to every type of scam, not just high-profile ones, and is also using AI to label new scam cases so its models learn from attacks within hours instead of weeks.

Social engineering has been a steady problem for Coinbase customers. In September, a Brooklyn man was sentenced to 12 years in prison over a $16 million Coinbase phishing scam. This week, Trezor customers reported scam calls after a breach at the hardware wallet maker’s shipping partner exposed 27,000 orders.

The post came the same day Coinbase launched a ChatGPT plugin for trading bitcoin, stocks and derivatives, which requires users to approve every order. Coinbase closed the post with a list of things it will never do, including promising to double, triple or multiply crypto that customers send.

“Nobody legitimate will double your crypto,” the company wrote.

Coinbase said its AI defenses blocked $4.7 million in attempted cryptocurrency transfers tied to an Elon Musk deepfake scam.

The crypto exchange said on Nov. 17 that its automated fraud-prevention system stopped about 91% of the money customers tried to send to scammers promoting a fake Tesla cryptocurrency giveaway.

The fraudsters had created a lookalike YouTube livestream during a Tesla demonstration, using an AI-generated impersonation of Musk to promise viewers twice the cryptocurrency they deposited into designated wallets.

More than 500,000 people watched the fraudulent broadcast, while hundreds of Coinbase customers attempted to transfer millions of dollars within roughly two hours.

Unlike conventional account compromises, the customers were willingly authorizing the transactions, believing they were participating in a legitimate promotion.

Coinbase said its AI system intercepted suspicious payments in real time, engaging customers before their funds could leave the platform without requiring human intervention.

Despite preventing most attempted transfers, Coinbase disclosed an incident that illustrates the difficulty of protecting customers determined to complete suspicious payments.

Will Megson, Coinbase's vice president of product working on risk, revealed that one customer initially attempted to transfer $100,000 to the scammers.

The exchange's AI agent identified the suspicious transaction, explained the fraudulent giveaway and convinced the customer to abandon the payment.

However, the customer subsequently returned and attempted another transfer, this time for $5,000.

#5057. Gonka AI Hit by $1 Million Exploit as Hacker Drains Stablecoins

Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and issue unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.

According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and issue Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.

Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.

Combined, the total value of the affected assets stood at around $1.06 million, per Onchain Lens.

Following the hack, the funds were transferred through the decentralized exchange Uniswap and multiple crypto wallets, making it challenging to trace their final destination.

The attack targeted Gonka AI's cross-chain bridge. The cross-chain bridge makes it possible to transfer assets from Gonka AI's native chain to Ethereum and vice versa.

According to the project's technical documentation, withdrawing funds from Gonka to Ethereum requires certain cryptographic signatures from the network's validator set.

The cryptographic signatures are checked against the BLS group key, which changes with every network epoch.

Per the report, the attacker was able to change the epoch BLS group key on the bridge, making it possible for the hacker to control the part of the bridge responsible for authorizing fund withdrawals.

Thus, the hacker was able to withdraw funds from the bridge's stablecoin reserves and issue WGNK tokens without locking the required amount of assets on the native blockchain.

Blockchain security firm Blockaid noted that the hack had taken place, with the total amount of funds stolen reaching about $1.05 million across roughly five transactions at the time of the initial alert.

At the time it spotted the suspicious activity, Blockaid noted that the hack was still ongoing.

Onchain Lens's numbers differ slightly, with the firm reporting around $884,800 in stablecoin withdrawals and $172,000 in unbacked WGNK issuance.

Notably, the issuance of unbacked tokens presents an additional problem, given that such tokens could potentially enter circulation without the necessary reserves to back them.

#5055. German Court Offers to Drop Movie2k Case for 40,000 Bitcoin

A Leipzig judge last week offered to dismiss the criminal case against the alleged operator of the defunct Movie2k piracy site if he hands over 40,000 bitcoin, a stake worth about $2.56 billion at current prices. The presiding judge at the Leipzig Regional Court, Karsten Nickel, made the proposal in a trial that began in February.

A spokesman for the Dresden prosecutors’ office confirmed it after German newspapers and the public broadcaster MDR first reported the offer. Heise later published a detailed account.

The trial is before the court’s economic criminal chamber, and the Leipzig court itself had not issued its own confirmation when prosecutors spoke to reporters. Prosecutors believe the defendant still holds about 56,000 bitcoin, and transferring 40,000 would leave him roughly 16,000 coins. At a bitcoin price of about $64,000, those 16,000 coins would be worth about $1.02 billion, and forty thousand bitcoin would be worth about $2.56 billion at the same price. The dollar figures are approximate.

The proposal also calls for him to pay €38 million in compensation for potential victims, including film rights holders, MDR reported. He would also have to give up any claim to the roughly €2.64 billion Saxony already raised from bitcoin he transferred in 2024, the newspaper Freie Presse reported. Even after handing over most of the remaining coins, he could leave court a billionaire.

Movie2k.to ran from 2008 until it was shut down in May 2013. Prosecutors say its operators made millions from advertising contracts and used the proceeds to buy bitcoin when the price was far lower. The defendant is charged with commercial money laundering in 146 cases. The court has already ruled that about 220,000 copyright counts are time-barred and are no longer part of the Movie2k case.

A co-defendant, a Polish national, is charged with money laundering in 46 cases and especially serious tax evasion. Prosecutors say he received bitcoin from the main defendant in May 2013 as pay for work on the site. Nickel has said that proof of some of the charges would face “great difficulties.” It is conceivable, he said, that legally and illegally obtained bitcoin were mixed in the accounts.

German authorities had sought the defendant internationally since late 2019. He was arrested abroad in May 2023 and held in pretrial detention in Saxony until mid-January 2024. On Jan. 16, 2024, he voluntarily transferred about 49,858 bitcoin to wallets provided by the Federal Criminal Police Office. At the time, the coins were worth about €1.96 billion, and he was released from detention around the time of that transfer.

Saxony sold the coins between June 19 and July 12, 2024, with support from the Federal Criminal Police Office, for €2,639,683,413.92, or about €2.64 billion. Prosecutors described the sale as an emergency liquidation required by bitcoin’s volatility. The proceeds are held by the state’s justice treasury and still belong to the defendant until there is a final confiscation ruling. Bitcoin Magazine has covered that sale.

Two other men in the Movie2k investigation were already convicted in 2023 and received suspended sentences. One was a co-operator of the site. The other handled payments.

A co-defendant in the Leipzig trial was offered terms of 600 bitcoin and €17 million, and his lawyer said she could imagine accepting that. The main defendant’s lawyers said they wanted to confer. The Dresden prosecutors’ office and the defense are still reviewing the Movie2k proposal, and neither side has announced a decision.

If both sides agree, the trial could end before Christmas. If they do not, the case will continue, and the court will still have to decide whether to confiscate the 2024 sale proceeds and any bitcoin he still holds.

#5053. Optimizely Hack Hijacked Ledger, BBC and 176 Other Sites to Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses

Optimizely Hack Hijacked Ledger, BBC and 176 Other Sites to Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses

An attacker hijacked Optimizely, a platform widely used by companies to run experiments on their websites, to serve malware that swapped visitors' crypto wallet addresses for their own, on sites including hardware wallet maker Ledger.

Optimizely said in a status update on Monday evening that an unauthorized party had exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. The company said it had fixed the flaw, removed the injected code, secured affected user accounts and added protections to stop unauthorized code being delivered.

Earlier today, Optimizely identified and contained a security incident affecting some Optimizely Web Experimentation customers. The vulnerable path is blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers have been contacted directly.

— Optimizely (@Optimizely) November 17, 2026

Researchers at security firm Report URI, which sells tools to detect malicious website scripts, found the malicious code in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts they examined, belonging to 178 organizations, according to a blog post by founder Scott Helme. The affected sites included Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA and HSBC, as well as crypto and trading firms such as Ledger, IG and OANDA.

Because the code was served from Optimizely's own trusted servers, affected websites loaded it without their own systems being breached.

The malware's main purpose was to steal crypto. The script scanned web pages for valid wallet addresses on networks including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana and TON, and replaced them with addresses controlled by the attacker, according to Report URI. It also swapped addresses copied to a user's clipboard, meaning anyone who copied an address while an affected page was open could have pasted the attacker's instead.

The attacker's wallets received about $7,150 in crypto, mostly in Bitcoin, Litecoin and USDT, according to Report URI's update on Tuesday. The attacker emptied the wallets early on Tuesday. One Tron address used to cash out had also been used in earlier operations in March and on November 3, allowing Report URI to link the attacker to other attacks, the firm said.

The script also skimmed card details typed into some sites' own payment forms, though not those entered into hosted payment fields such as Stripe's, and on iPhones and iPads it attempted to load exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword, which target older versions of iOS. Report URI said it could not see how many card numbers were stolen or how many devices were compromised.

The injected code first appeared early on November 16 UTC, and had been removed from all of the scripts Report URI could find by late that evening.

Optimizely spokesperson Victoria Johnson told Gizmodo that an unauthorized party had "exploited a vulnerability in the Experimentation account signup flow," and that the company had blocked access to the vulnerable path, deployed a fix and notified all affected customers. The company has not said how the attacker gained access to other customers' projects.

Helme said visitors to affected sites on November 16 should check any crypto transfers they made, update their iPhones and iPads, and watch their card statements. Website operators should review custom code in their Optimizely projects and rotate credentials, he added.

#5052. Can AI Hack Smart Contracts? How AI Agents Are Changing Blockchain Security

Smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns. However, because an AI agent can iterate and make use of dependencies, local blockchain forks, and decompilation, it weakens the protection gained by keeping source code secret, and can attempt attacks against complex vulnerabilities such as access control bugs, accounting errors, oracle-related bugs and unexpected contract interactions.

For example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period. They were able to reproduce exploits for 207 contracts, totalling $550.1 million (simulated stolen funds).

To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).

Finally, they analysed 2,849 recent smart contracts with no known issues, discovering two previously unknown vulnerabilities that could have resulted in $3,694 (simulated stolen funds), emphasising the ability of AI agents to discover new vulnerabilities rather than simply exploiting known ones.

Anthropic emphasised that no actual funds were lost during these experiments. It should also be noted that in one of their experiments using GPT-5, it cost $3,476 for API usage, which leaves a slim (simulated) profit.

With automated hacking becoming more effective, how can we be sure that DeFi will be able to stay ahead of these AI agents? Hacken, a blockchain security firm, reported that $1.18 billion was lost in 107 crypto hacks during the third quarter of 2026. 48% of this was from exploiting smart contracts.

Of course, this doesn’t specify the cause of these hacks. Regardless, it emphasises the importance of being able to stay ahead of AIs which could be used for exploitation.

Chainalysis estimates that approximately $36.7 million was stolen in 2026 from DeFi protocols that had not undergone smart contract verification. It also notes AI-assisted reverse engineering as an emerging risk without attributing any particular thefts to AI.

In an experiment by a16z on 20 past DeFi price manipulation exploits, apparent success rates of 50% were reduced to 10% when the researchers restricted access to transactional data that revealed the original exploit. When the researchers gave the AI some high-level information about the DeFi domain, success rates jumped to 70%.

In February 2026, OpenAI and Paradigm released a benchmark for evaluating agents’ abilities in the domains of vulnerability detection, patching, and exploitation using an EVM environment (EVMbench). Results showed that GPT-5.3-Codex achieved a 71% success rate in exploitation (limited to a sandboxed environment) and 33.3% for GPT-5.

In October 2026, CyberChainBench was released, analyzing 541 exploit events across 9 Ethereum-compatible blockchains. The best-performing configuration achieved 37.5%, 43.7%, and 23.4% success rates for detection, exploitation, and patching respectively.

In a simulation, the best-performing agent profited $57.4 million from exploits on 200 exploit events that occurred after the cutoff. Some of the reported high-severity issues were evaluated and determined to not be exploitable by OpenZeppelin. Since much of the data is trained on in the public, results may be exaggerated.

Agents will continue to improve, and while current results are not an indication that AI-driven agents are responsible for large scale on-chain thefts, it is an indication that AI can find and exploit weaknesses in smart contracts given a certain environment. Given the ease with which agents can try attacking many different protocols, smaller protocols may see an uptick in exploit attempts.

Teams that implement rigorous testing and monitoring could have an edge over other teams. For example, AI could be used to test a contract prior to deployment, generate regression tests, and identify weird behavior on-chain. A human would still need to verify any potential issues and sign off on changes.

Teams should continue to perform third-party audits and implement other security best practices such as limiting access to sensitive information, setting up alerts and response plans, restricting the amount of money in a wallet, making sure AI systems do not have permissions to transact without human oversight where necessary, and so on.

#5050. Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout

Ionic Digital (IOND) sold about 737 bitcoin after the end of September for roughly $61.6 million and plans to spend the money building out its data center sites, the miner built from Celsius’ old mining business disclosed in its latest quarterly report. The company said in its 10-Q that the coins sold at an average of $83,600 each, net of trading costs. The sales cut its bitcoin holdings by about 25% from the Sept. 30 balance.

Ionic held 2,954 bitcoin at the end of the third quarter, up from 2,719 at the end of 2025. That implies about 2,217 bitcoin left after the sales. “The Company intends to use the proceeds to fund the development of its existing data center sites,” the filing said.

The filing does not say when the coins were sold. Bitcoin traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, about 23% below Ionic’s average sale price.

Ionic was formed in January 2024 to take over the assets of Celsius Mining under the bankrupt lender’s Chapter 11 plan. It started out as a pure bitcoin miner, running fleets of ASIC machines at its own and hosted sites. That changed in October 2025, when it signed a lease with a single tenant for its Ward County, Texas, facility, which it previously called Cedarvale. The lease runs through January 2037.

The third quarter shows how far the shift has gone, with revenue rising to about $49.0 million from $37.1 million a year earlier. Digital infrastructure leasing brought in $43.9 million of that, while mining revenue fell to $5.1 million from $37.1 million.

Ionic swung to a net profit of $17.4 million for the quarter, compared with a $4.5 million loss a year earlier. That result included a $73.2 million gain on the fair value of its bitcoin, offset in part by a $65.9 million loss from remeasuring warrants. For the first nine months of the year, Ionic posted a net loss of $30.9 million.

In February, Ionic amended the Ward County lease. The tenant is now obligated to lease another 89 megawatts of capacity when it becomes available. Control of that added capacity had not passed to the tenant by the end of September, so Ionic has not booked any revenue on it. The company also had about $19.6 million left to pay on transformer purchases and a substation expansion at the site.

The conversion has cost Ionic mining capacity. The company said it does not have room at its owned and leased sites to relocate all of the miners it used to run, so it has decommissioned some of them. Ionic went public through a direct listing on July 28 and raised $400 million in a private placement before $16.7 million in costs. It had about $381.4 million in cash and equivalents at Sept. 30.

Ionic is one of several public miners turning bitcoin into cash for AI and data center projects this month. MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin for $1.1 billion and said more sales were coming. Core Scientific plans to exit bitcoin mining by year-end, and Hyperscale Data sold its last bitcoin to fund an AI data center.

Ionic’s sale is smaller, but the share is large. A quarter of its treasury is now going into the data center buildout. The company still mines. In July, it moved its hashrate from Foundry to Luxor’s mining pool, and mining added about $5.1 million worth of bitcoin to its holdings in the third quarter.

The test now is whether the 89 megawatts come online fast enough to justify selling coins that would fetch about $14 million less at Wednesday’s price.

#5049. 'The Biggest Opportunity in Crypto Is Already Underway': Solana Bets Big on AI Agents

'The Biggest Opportunity in Crypto Is Already Underway': Solana Bets Big on AI Agents

AI agents are becoming the internet's main users, and the Solana Foundation wants its blockchain to be how they pay for things.

"The biggest opportunity in crypto is already underway," Rishin Sharma, who leads AI at the Solana Foundation, said at the Breakpoint conference in London.

Sharma used his presentation to showcase Solana.ai, a new homepage for the network's AI ecosystem, which the foundation launched last week. More than 120 teams are now building AI products on Solana across payments, trading and infrastructure, he said.

Bots and other automated software accounted for more than 53% of global web traffic in 2025, up from 51% the year before, according to cybersecurity firm Imperva's latest Bad Bot Report, which Sharma cited. Agents have also come to dominate AI usage: API keys classified as agentic accounted for 76% of the tokens processed through model marketplace OpenRouter in October 2026, up from 8% a year earlier, according to the company's monthly data recap.

At the same time, AI is getting much cheaper. Sharma's slides showed the price of a million tokens falling from $37.50 for GPT-4 to $0.14 for GPT-5 nano, a 270-fold drop, while monthly token use has risen around 330-fold.

"Which model is smarter matters a little bit less, and what matters more is what the model can actually do," Sharma said. "What are the tools it's using? What are the data it's able to access? And what money can it functionally use?"

Payments are where that shift is showing up first, Sharma said. The x402 standard, which lets AI agents pay for online services, has processed more than 400 million payments and $100 million in volume, up from zero a year ago, he said. Solana-based BlockRun, which he described as the largest x402 server, has handled more than 60 million transactions in the past two months.

The foundation has also launched payment channels that it says can handle 1 million payments per second, a private AI service offering attested private inference on Solana, and Pay.sh, a server integrating more than 100 APIs that agents can pay for, Sharma said. He added that the foundation is working with companies including Google, Alibaba and ByteDance to let them charge for their AI models through agent payments.

Next, the foundation plans to publish benchmarks for how well AI models perform financial tasks, and to launch an on-ramp that lets users convert cash to stablecoins and hand them to their AI assistants, he said.

Macro investor and Real Vision founder Raoul Pal, speaking earlier at the conference, argued that agents are not yet real economic actors. "They're like kids," he said. "These are young kids who spend nothing on a few sweets and stuff." But as stocks and other assets move onchain, he said, agents will start using blockchains to trade and settle, and "the value accrues to the underlying layer one."

Solana has been building toward this for months. The foundation teamed up with Google Cloud on a stablecoin payments service for AI agents in May, while the x402 Foundation, backed by Coinbase and the Linux Foundation, is developing the payments standard. Franklin Templeton has described agentic AI as a killer use case for crypto.

A trader borrowing yen short-term to hold Bitcoin faces higher costs to renew the loan if funding rates rise. If the trader sells Bitcoin for dollars and leaves the yen debt unhedged, a stronger yen makes repaying the loan in dollar terms more expensive.

Bank for International Settlements researchers documented that feedback during the August 2024 unwind in leveraged currency and equity trades.

Bitfinex reported that aggregate Bitcoin futures open interest fell to 645,750 BTC over Nov. 14 and 15, 8% below Nov. 11. The futures total shows how much exposure was outstanding but gives no breakdown by funding currency.

The Finance Ministry plans to offer about ¥300 billion at the Nov. 25 reopening of a 40-year bond, the next test of long-dated demand.

A stronger signal for Bitcoin would be rising short-term yen borrowing costs or a sustained strengthening of the yen, alongside shrinking futures exposure and evidence that traders cutting positions had yen liabilities.

#5047. Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’

K33 Research said bitcoin is trading in “deep value territory” after a 14% weekly drop, arguing that “any entry below $70K is a gift from the market” for medium- to long-term investors.

The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov. 16. Head of research Vetle Lunde wrote that bitcoin’s slide has erased its August and September gains and left the market deeply oversold. Bitcoin has posted six straight red weekly candles and is on track for a record 13 consecutive days of lower daily highs, according to K33.

Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan. 26 to March 1, 2026, and from April 3 to May 29, 2022. Daily RSI, a momentum gauge, hit 19.95 on Saturday and has stayed below 25 since Friday. Bitcoin also fell below its 200-week moving average, near $68,000, after its worst weekly return since June 7.

At the bottom on Nov. 15, bitcoin traded about 8.5% under the 200-week average, a wider gap than the 7.3% recorded at June’s low of $58,500. K33 said 51.5% of the bitcoin supply last moved on-chain at prices above the current level, meaning the average holder could have sold for more at some point in the past four years.

Lunde said those readings, taken together, have typically lined up with market bottoms. K33 also noted that crypto has lagged traditional markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recovering modestly last week while bitcoin sank.

Bitcoin was trading near $62,300 on Wednesday, according to Coinbase spot prices, below the roughly $65,000 level cited in the K33 report, which showed bitcoin down 14% on the week and about 20% over 30 days. Ether also fell 14% over the week, to around $1,827.

Capital continues to leave bitcoin funds. Net outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded products reached 44,900 BTC over the 14 trading days since Oct. 29, K33 said, short of the record of about 71,000 BTC set in June. Total ETF holdings fell to about 1.46 million BTC, the lowest since Aug. 19, and leveraged ETF exposure dropped to 21,900 BTC, the lowest since March 2024.

Forced selling hit derivatives, too. About $1.3 billion in long positions were liquidated on Nov. 13 and 14 as bitcoin broke below $70,000, K33 said, and funding rates on perpetual futures repeatedly turned negative. Open interest fell by about 30,000 BTC but stayed above 330,000 BTC, leaving leverage elevated against historical norms.

Institutional futures players largely stayed on the sidelines. Open interest in bitcoin futures on CME stayed below 100,000 BTC all week, K33 said, a sign that regulated-market participants have not rushed in to buy the dip.

Demand for downside protection is also surging. The one-month 25-delta skew, which compares the price of puts to calls, rose above 20 for the first time since July, a level Lunde said has historically coincided with “selling exhaustion near local bottoms.”

Stablecoins offer another sign of stress. K33 said net redemptions totaled $16.1 billion over the past month, the largest outflow since the collapse of Terra.

Lunde stopped short of calling the decline over. He said earlier recoveries from similar conditions involved “prolonged consolidation,” pointing to a choppy recovery rather than an immediate rebound.

There were some constructive signs in trading activity. Spot volume ran near $5 billion a day from Friday through Sunday, the busiest weekend since February, which K33 said could give the market firmer footing after weeks of one-way selling.

Even so, leverage remains high, and ETF money is still heading out the door. Bitcoin was near $62,300 at the time of writing, below the roughly $68,000 200-week average K33 flagged as a key level.
